# Context Engine — Phase 1 Parameter Matrix (RAW, 14 lenses)

*Self-generated by 14 blind first-principles lenses (2026-06-23), grounded in the real repo + 2026 tech + the IPP poster. 195 parameters. This is the RAW per-lens output; the cross-lens dedup/synthesis was the one step that got cut off by usage limits (reconstruct it from this file — no need to re-run agents). Companion: `CONTEXT_ENGINE_GROUNDING_2026-06-23.md`.*


## Acquisition physics — sensors, FOV, optics, frame/audio cadence, motion blur, rolling shutter, lighting, exposure, multi-camera, what is physically capturable

### acq-1 — Sharpness/blur is never measured — only inter-frame change is ⚠️
- **Why:** The whole text-recall moat (consensus OCR, 47%->60%) assumes the frames it reads are in focus. But the only 'quality' signal in the live pipeline is frameMotion (ContentView.swift:2153), an L1 difference of a downsampled luma fingerprint between consecutive frames. That measures CHANGE, not SHARPNESS. A frame can score 'stable' (motion<0.08, scenePhase=stable) while being uniformly motion-blurred (panning slowly) or defocused, and that blurry frame is exactly what gets promoted to the expensive accurateOCR/VLM pass.
- **Failure if ignored:** OCR runs on confidently-blurry stable frames; consensus then votes a garbled read into 'high frequency = high confidence' and launders a hallucination through the honesty gate. The honesty moat is blind to optical quality.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On a held-out walk, what fraction of frames that pass the stable-gate (motion<0.08) have a per-frame focus metric (variance-of-Laplacian / VNDetectDocumentSegmentation sharpness) below the OCR-usable threshold? I.e. what is the false-stable rate, and does adding a real sharpness gate move strict text-recall above the current 60%?
- **Current-tech hook:** Variance-of-Laplacian over the existing luma plane in frameFingerprint costs microseconds on ANE; Apple Vision exposes per-observation confidence already used by consensus — gate OCR on a true sharpness score before the still-capture/OCR spend, not on frame-difference.

### acq-2 — Rolling-shutter + walking-pace skew corrupts verbatim text geometry ⚠️
- **Why:** AVCaptureVideoDataOutput on iPhone CMOS reads line-by-line (rolling shutter). At walking pace with hand sway, vertical signage and straight text baselines shear/wobble within a single exposure. accurateOCR (CaptureV2.swift:57) and Vision OCR assume roughly rectilinear glyphs; the product's core promise is verbatim signs/screens/badges — the exact content most sensitive to shear.
- **Failure if ignored:** Station signs, room numbers and badge IDs OCR with transposed/dropped characters specifically when the user is moving — the dominant capture mode for an ambient walking device — and consensus can't fix a systematically skewed read because every frame shares the same distortion direction.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Quantify character-error-rate on the same physical sign captured (a) while stationary vs (b) while walking at ~1.4 m/s, on the device's actual sensor. Does the dwell-triggered full-res STILL path (photoOutput, global-ish/optimized capture) measurably beat the streaming-buffer path for the same sign?
- **Current-tech hook:** The repo already has a still path (CameraController.captureStill, photoQualityPrioritization=max) distinct from the stream buffer; iPhone 16 sensors expose AVCaptureDevice min ISO/exposure-duration to cap exposure time and freeze motion. Neither is currently tuned for text capture.

### acq-3 — Exposure/auto-gain is uncontrolled — bright signs and screens blow out ⚠️
- **Why:** Nothing in CameraController sets exposureMode, custom exposure duration, or metering region. The session runs full-auto. The highest-value text targets are emissive (phone/monitor/departure-board screens) and backlit signage; auto-exposure metered for the whole scene routinely clips these to white or crushes them when the surround is bright (outdoor) or dark (indoor screen at night).
- **Failure if ignored:** The single most answerable, highest-value reads — a screen the user is looking at, a lit station board — are precisely the ones that clip and become unreadable, so the honest channel refuses on exactly the queries a user most expects to work.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Across a capture set of emissive text targets (phone screen, monitor, LED board) under 3 ambient levels, what is OCR success with default auto-exposure vs. a text-target exposure mode (spot-metered / capped EV on the detected text bbox)? How much recall is left on the table by not controlling exposure?
- **Current-tech hook:** AVCaptureDevice supports setExposureModeCustom and setExposurePointOfInterest; YOLO11n/Vision already gives a text/object bbox to meter on. HDR/Smart-HDR is on by default but tuned for photos, not legible small text.

### acq-4 — Fixed wide FOV + no optical zoom caps the legible-text distance ⚠️
- **Why:** The back camera runs a single fixed lens at hd1920x1080. There is no zoom/tele selection and no per-target crop-before-OCR. Glyph legibility is governed by pixels-on-the-character: a sign across a platform or a room-number above a door subtends too few pixels to OCR even if perfectly sharp and exposed. The product implicitly promises 'a memory for everything you read,' but physics bounds 'read' to a distance/character-height envelope nobody has measured.
- **Failure if ignored:** Users assume the device read a distant sign it physically couldn't resolve; the system either refuses (frustrating) or the VLM guesses (hallucination). The capability boundary is invisible and unstated.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the legibility envelope — minimum character angular size (pixels per glyph) at which Vision OCR holds >90% accuracy on this sensor — and therefore the max real-world distance for a 5 cm vs 30 cm sign? What fraction of a real walk's signage falls outside it?
- **Current-tech hook:** iPhone 16 Pro has a 5x tele and supports multi-cam; AVCaptureMultiCamSession could pull a tele crop for distant text. ROI-crop-then-upscale on the wide frame is a cheaper near-term lever. None is wired today.

### acq-5 — Frame cadence (every 4s sim / dwell-gated native) vs. transient text exposure ⚠️
- **Why:** The Mac spine samples every 4.0s (trace_live_feed.py:227); the native path only escalates to expensive OCR after 8s of accumulated DWELL on a track (EnrichmentScheduler dwellBaseSeconds=8). Ambient walking text is often transient: a sign passes through frame in <2s, a glanced screen, a badge in a doorway. A dwell-and-cadence model structurally MISSES anything the user didn't linger on.
- **Failure if ignored:** The device systematically captures only what the user stared at, not what they 'read' in passing — contradicting the 'memory for everything you read' promise. Worse, missed-but-glanced items leave no provenance, so later the LLM can't even honestly say 'I saw it briefly.'
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the dwell/cadence vs. recall curve: for text that appears for T seconds in frame, what is capture probability at the current 4s sample / 8s dwell, and where is the knee? How much does an opportunistic 'text-detected -> grab a still NOW' interrupt (bypassing dwell) improve transient-sign recall, and at what thermal/battery cost?
- **Current-tech hook:** A lightweight VNDetectTextRectangles pre-pass at low res can fire a still capture the instant text enters frame, decoupling text capture from the person-dwell salience model that currently gates enrichment.

### acq-6 — Motion fingerprint resolution sets the smallest detectable change — and it's tuned for scenes, not text ⚠️
- **Why:** frameFingerprint downsamples the luma plane to a small grid; the motion score is mean absolute grid difference / 255 (ContentView.swift:2159). The grid resolution determines what counts as 'stable.' A small but decisive change — a departure board flipping one row, a screen updating a number — produces near-zero global fingerprint delta and is judged 'no change,' so no fresh OCR fires; conversely whole-frame lighting flicker reads as 'motion' and suppresses capture.
- **Failure if ignored:** Dynamic text surfaces (the high-value emissive targets from acq-3) update under the stability radar and the memory goes stale while reporting 'stable' — the user asks 'what's the next train' and gets the read from 40s ago, presented as current.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** At the current fingerprint grid size, what is the minimum on-screen text change (rows of a board, % of frame) that crosses the motion>0.08 threshold? Does a text-region-localized change detector (diff only inside detected text bboxes) catch board/screen updates the global fingerprint misses?
- **Current-tech hook:** Region-restricted frame differencing over Vision text-rectangle bboxes is cheap and already has the bboxes; this turns 'global stable' into 'this sign changed' for staleness control.

### acq-7 — Stale-comment / config drift: VGA assumed, HD1080 actually captured ⚠️
- **Why:** setupCaptureSession sets sessionPreset = .hd1920x1080 (CameraController.swift:216), but ContentView.swift:464 still asserts 'Because we're using the AVCaptureSession preset .vga640x480' and hardcodes a 4:3 aspectRatio and the detector bridge falls back to a 640-pt normalization (TraceDetectorBridge.swift:269). The capture resolution the rest of the pipeline believes it has does not match reality.
- **Failure if ignored:** Bbox normalization, crop math, and aspect-ratio rendering are computed against the wrong frame dimensions, mis-locating text/object ROIs — which corrupts any ROI-crop-before-OCR and any pose/bbox provenance. Silent, systematic spatial error in exactly the geometry the spatial-graph workstream depends on.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Audit: what is the ACTUAL CVPixelBuffer width/height/aspect delivered on the target device for the live stream vs. the still path, and does any consumer (detector normalization, aspectRatio, crop) assume 640x480 / 4:3? Fix and re-measure ROI alignment error.
- **Current-tech hook:** CVPixelBufferGetWidth/Height at runtime resolves it definitively; this is a today-fixable correctness bug, not a research question.

### acq-8 — Single mic, no array — speech capture has no spatial selectivity or noise rejection ⚠️
- **Why:** The ASR helpers (SpeechAnalyzer/whisper) are real-time and accurate IN CLEAN AUDIO, but capture is a single undifferentiated mic stream. On a real walk — wind, traffic, café babble, the user's own footfalls/clothing rustle on a chest/pocket-worn device — there is no beamforming toward a speaker and no own-voice vs. other-voice separation. WER numbers (2.2%) are read-aloud lab numbers, not ambient-walk numbers.
- **Failure if ignored:** Transcript channel emits confident but wrong speech in noise, or floods the injection layer with overheard bystander speech the user never 'heard,' creating false 'I heard X' memories. The honesty moat covers OCR refusal but there's no acoustic-SNR refusal.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is real-walk WER vs. lab WER for this capture rig, and what SNR floor should trigger an honest 'audio too noisy' refusal? Does multi-mic beamforming / own-voice detection (who is speaking) materially change usable transcript yield?
- **Current-tech hook:** iPhone has a 3-mic array; AVAudioSession supports beamforming and Apple's Voice Isolation; SFSpeechRecognition exposes per-segment confidence that could drive an acoustic refusal threshold the system currently ignores.

### acq-9 — Thermal duty-cycle directly starves the capture rate within ~1 minute ⚠️
- **Why:** The EnrichmentScheduler already scales budget by thermalState (1.0/0.7/0.4/0.1) — an honest acknowledgment that sustained capture is thermally impossible (~4-5W sustained, throttle in ~60s). But that means the device's effective frame/OCR/VLM cadence DEGRADES the longer it runs, and degrades most in hot conditions (outdoors, in a bag). Capture coverage is a function of temperature, not just the scene.
- **Failure if ignored:** A demo that works for 60s collapses in a 10-minute real walk: enrichment tokens drop to 10%, OCR fires rarely, the memory thins out — and nothing tells the user 'I'm running hot and capturing less,' so gaps look like the product 'not noticing' things.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Plot effective OCR/VLM passes-per-minute vs. wall-clock over a sustained 15-min outdoor walk on the actual device. At what minute does the thermal scale cross into 'serious' (0.4x), and what is the recall loss between minute 1 and minute 12?
- **Current-tech hook:** ProcessInfo.thermalState is already read; the missing piece is honest user-facing capture-rate signaling and pushing more perception (OCR/ASR/embeddings) onto the ANE — which throttles far less than the GPU/VLM path the scheduler is protecting.

### acq-10 — No light-level / low-light refusal — dark-frame guessing ⚠️
- **Why:** Indoor evenings, transit, dusk: at low lux the sensor pushes ISO and exposure time up, amplifying noise and motion blur simultaneously. Nothing reads the scene luminance to decide capture is futile; the pipeline forwards a noisy, smeared frame to OCR/VLM all the same, and the VLM (gemma3) will still emit a confident SCENE/TEXT line.
- **Failure if ignored:** Low-light frames produce maximum-hallucination conditions (noise patterns read as glyphs), and there is no acquisition-side gate to refuse before the read even happens — the honesty layer has to clean up a mess the capture layer should have prevented.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What scene-luminance / sensor-ISO threshold predicts OCR failure, and would a capture-side low-light refusal (skip OCR, mark 'too dark') reduce hallucination rate more cheaply than downstream consensus filtering?
- **Current-tech hook:** AVCaptureDevice.exposureTargetOffset / ISO / lensAperture are readable per frame; a simple luma-histogram gate on the existing fingerprint plane gives a free 'too dark to read honestly' signal.

### acq-11 — OCR language set is hardcoded (en-US, de-DE) — out-of-set scripts silently degrade ⚠️
- **Why:** accurateOCR fixes recognitionLanguages to ['en-US','de-DE'] (CaptureV2.swift:62) with usesLanguageCorrection=true. For an ambient device that goes anywhere, any other script (CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic, accented FR/ES/IT) is either unrecognized or, worse, language-correction snaps a foreign string toward an English/German word — a quiet fabrication baked in at the OCR call, upstream of every honesty check.
- **Failure if ignored:** Verbatim promise breaks for non-EN/DE text: signs get auto-corrected into plausible English garbage that then passes consensus (it's stable across frames) and the gate (it's literally in the corpus). The lie is manufactured at acquisition.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On out-of-set-language signage, what is the rate of (a) miss vs. (b) language-correction-induced fabrication, and does disabling usesLanguageCorrection (or auto-detecting script first) trade recall for a real reduction in fabricated reads?
- **Current-tech hook:** VNRecognizeTextRequest supports automaticallyDetectsLanguage and a wider recognitionLanguages set on recent iOS; Vision also exposes supportedRecognitionLanguages to bound the honest claim.

### acq-12 — No timestamp/clock-skew model across helper streams — fusion binds the wrong moment ⚠️
- **Why:** Vision frames, ASR segments, CoreLocation hints, and detector tracks arrive on independent clocks and latencies (ASR commits seconds after the audio; geocode is async; VLM TTFT is seconds). The injection layer fuses 'co-occurring' observations, but if frame-T's OCR is bound to speech that was actually uttered 3s earlier (or a GPS hint from 5s ago), it builds a false episode. This is an acquisition-timing problem before it's a fusion problem.
- **Failure if ignored:** Cross-modal binding (WS4) stitches a sign, an overheard sentence, and a place that were never simultaneous into one 'episode,' producing confidently-wrong recall ('you read X while she said Y at place Z') with full provenance — the most dangerous kind because it looks grounded.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What are the actual end-to-end latencies and jitter of each capture channel (frame->OCR, mic->committed-ASR, GPS->geocoded-place) on-device, and what time-alignment window keeps cross-modal binding precision above an acceptable false-co-occurrence rate?
- **Current-tech hook:** CMSampleBuffer presentationTimeStamp and SFTranscription segment timestamps give true media-time; binding on media-time rather than wall-clock-arrival fixes the skew — but nothing currently aligns them.


## Compute / thermal / power / memory

### thermal-1 — Sustained-power ceiling vs. the helper fan-out (the melt budget) ⚠️
- **Why:** The whole thesis is N parallel always-on perceivers (VLM keyframe, Vision OCR, SpeechAnalyzer/Whisper, detector+tracker, location, embeddings). Each is individually cheap but the architecture's defining feature is that they run CONCURRENTLY and CONTINUOUSLY. The A18 Pro peaks 8-10W but sustains only ~4-5W before throttling; camera+ANE+CPU for a perceiver swarm easily blows that. The repo has a per-VLM-call TokenBucket but NO global power accountant summing all live channels.
- **Failure if ignored:** Device throttles in ~1 minute, frame rate collapses, helpers start dropping observations silently, consensus quorum can never be met (frequency=confidence breaks because frequency drops), and the 'ambient/continuous' claim becomes 'works for 60 seconds then degrades'. The honesty moat inverts: degraded helpers don't refuse, they just emit less, so the brain sees thin evidence and the gate over-refuses.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** With all live helpers running concurrently on the target iPhone (16 Pro / A18 Pro), what is the measured sustained SoC package power (W) and the wall-clock time-to-first-throttle at 22C ambient? Does total continuous draw stay under ~4.5W sustained, and if not, which helpers must duty-cycle?
- **Current-tech hook:** A18 Pro sustains ~4-5W, throttles ~1 min into intensive AR/camera compute (Apple ARKit capture-frame-rate-throttling doc). Repo's TokenBucket.applyThermalState (EnrichmentScheduler.swift:111) only scales the VLM budget, not OCR/ASR/embeddings/detector — there is no aggregate power governor.

### thermal-2 — Thermal state is read but not closed-loop across all channels ⚠️
- **Why:** ProcessInfo.thermalState is sampled and mapped to a VLM budget scale (1.0/0.7/0.4/0.1 at nominal/fair/serious/critical), but OCR, ASR, the detector tick rate, embedding cadence, and capture FPS are NOT bound to the same signal. A real thermal control loop has to throttle EVERY duty-cycled consumer proportionally, and it must react to thermalState BEFORE .critical (by .critical the OS is already shedding your work for you).
- **Failure if ignored:** Only the VLM backs off under heat while OCR/ASR/detector keep hammering the ANE/CPU; the device still melts, the VLM (your best perceiver) is starved first and worst, and you lose scene understanding exactly when you've already lost it. Asymmetric throttling makes the perceiver mix lopsided and the fusion layer blind in a predictable way.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Is there a single thermal-governor that scales capture FPS, OCR cadence, ASR window, detector tick, and embedding batch together as one budget? Measure: at .serious thermalState, what is each channel's actual duty cycle, and does aggregate draw actually fall to a sustainable level or just shuffle load between blocks?
- **Current-tech hook:** Repo maps thermalState only inside TokenBucket (EnrichmentScheduler.swift:111-119) governing VLM enrichment grants; no equivalent governor on the Vision OCR / SpeechAnalyzer / detector paths in TraceLiveContextEngines.swift / CaptureV2.swift.

### thermal-3 — Model residency vs. swap — keeping multiple models hot in unified memory ⚠️
- **Why:** Continuous context needs the VLM (FastVLM 0.5B-7B), the ASR model (Whisper base ~150MB / SpeechAnalyzer), the detector (YOLO), the embedding model (MiniLM), plus OCR — all resident SIMULTANEOUSLY to avoid load latency on every tick. On an 8GB iPhone with a hard per-app memory limit (jetsam), they can't all stay hot; cold-loading a VLM per keyframe adds seconds of TTFT and burns power. This is a memory-RESIDENCY scheduling problem the repo doesn't model.
- **Failure if ignored:** iOS jetsam kills the app under memory pressure (the worst possible failure for an always-on memory product — the memory dies), OR models get evicted and every keyframe pays a multi-second reload, destroying the live duty cycle and spiking power from repeated cold loads.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the steady-state resident-set size (RSS) with FastVLM + Whisper/SpeechAnalyzer + YOLO + MiniLM all loaded on an 8GB device, and how close is it to the per-app jetsam limit? Which models can stay hot vs. must be lazy-loaded, and what is the cold-load TTFT penalty per model?
- **Current-tech hook:** FastVLM 0.5B weights public but Apple hid absolutes; moondream2 4-bit ~4s TTFT on iPhone 14 shows cold-VLM cost. iOS per-app memory limits + jetsam are the hard wall; repo TraceLocalRuntime.swift only checks model files EXIST (:39-64), nothing about co-residency or RSS budget.

### thermal-4 — Battery Wh per active hour — the user-facing 'how long can I wear it' number
- **Why:** Ambient/continuous is a wearable-class promise. The actual product constraint isn't tok/s, it's how many hours of continuous capture the phone battery survives and how hot it gets in a pocket/mount. Camera + ANE + display-off continuous capture is a heavy drain; nobody in the repo has measured mWh/min for the full live stack. Without this number you cannot make any honest 'all-day memory' claim.
- **Failure if ignored:** Product promises 'ambient all-day' but the phone is dead in 2-3 hours and uncomfortably hot, OR the user must keep it plugged in (killing the wearable story). Pitch claim collapses on first real-world trial; this is exactly the Humane/Rabbit failure pattern the thesis claims to beat.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Measured: battery drain in Wh (or % per hour) for the full continuous live stack on the target device, screen off, in a realistic carry, at 22C — and the resulting continuous runtime hours and peak skin temperature?
- **Current-tech hook:** A18 Pro 8-10W peak / 4-5W sustained against a ~12-15Wh iPhone battery implies single-digit-hour ceilings under sustained perception. No power/battery telemetry exists in scripts/ or native (grep: thermal hits are unrelated build scripts).

### thermal-5 — VLM duty-cycle ratio is the master throughput knob, and it's salience-gated not power-gated ⚠️
- **Why:** The repo's EnrichmentScheduler is genuinely good: salience-scored, ladder (overview/attributes/minutiae at 8/24/72s dwell), hourly token ceiling. But the ceiling (basePerHour) is a fixed design constant scaled only by thermalState — it is NOT derived from a measured per-call energy cost. You cannot set the right basePerHour until you know joules-per-VLM-call and your power budget. Right now the most expensive helper's rate is a guessed magic number.
- **Failure if ignored:** basePerHour set too high → melts (see thermal-1); set too low → the VLM almost never fires, the brain runs on OCR+detector only, and the 'rich scene understanding' degrades to text-recall (which the memory notes already admit is the honest wedge). Either way the number was picked by feel, not by an energy budget.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the measured energy-per-VLM-call (J) at each ladder level for FastVLM-0.5B on-device, and what basePerHour (calls/hour) keeps the VLM's share of the power budget under its allocation while still hitting useful enrichment coverage?
- **Current-tech hook:** Ladder + TokenBucket basePerHour in EnrichmentScheduler.swift (dwell 8/24/72s, scale 0.4 at .serious); basePerHour is injected as a constant with no energy-cost derivation. FastVLM absolutes unpublished → must benchmark J/call locally first.

### thermal-6 — Consensus/frequency-as-confidence is silently coupled to thermal duty cycle ⚠️
- **Why:** The validated honesty mechanism (consensus_recall.py: frequency=vote-weight, refuse below quorum; structured_recall MIN_REPEAT_SUPPORT>=2) ASSUMES the helper fired enough times to vote. Under throttling, capture FPS and VLM/OCR cadence drop, so the same real-world fact gets observed fewer times — its frequency falls below quorum and the system refuses a fact it actually saw. Thermal state is thus a hidden input to the correctness layer nobody has modeled.
- **Failure if ignored:** Recall quality is silently temperature-dependent: cool device = answers; hot/throttled device = 'NOT IN MEMORY' for things it genuinely perceived. Demos pass cold and fail warm. The honesty moat becomes a thermometer, and a reviewer can't reproduce results because they depend on ambient temp and battery state.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** How does effective observation-frequency-per-real-fact change between .nominal and .serious thermalState, and does the quorum threshold (MIN_REPEAT_SUPPORT, consensus quorum) need to be normalized by current duty cycle rather than being an absolute count?
- **Current-tech hook:** consensus_recall.py:144 (tally[k]+=mult), structured_recall MIN_REPEAT_SUPPORT>=2 — fixed absolute repeat counts. Thermal throttling reduces capture/enrich cadence (ARKit throttling doc), directly lowering achievable repeat counts. Coupling is unmodeled.

### thermal-7 — Memory growth of the append-only log + vector store on a phone with no eviction ⚠️
- **Why:** Founder's perfect-recall decision: 'never delete a memory; decay = retrieval cost, not deletion.' On-device, every observation appends NDJSON (appendNativePayload) + a vector to sqlite-vec. sqlite-vec is BRUTE-FORCE (no HNSW/IVF), so query cost grows LINEARLY with lifetime observation count. Continuous capture for weeks/months = hundreds of thousands of vectors = full-table scan per recall = growing latency AND growing energy per query on a thermally constrained device.
- **Failure if ignored:** Recall latency and energy creep upward forever; what's snappy in a demo (1 day of data) is sluggish and battery-hungry after a month. Storage fills the phone. The 'never delete' principle, correct in spirit, becomes a thermal/latency time-bomb because the index is linear-scan.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** At realistic capture rates, how many vectors/day accumulate, and what is sqlite-vec brute-force query latency + energy at 100k / 500k / 1M vectors on-device? At what N does recall exceed an acceptable latency/energy budget, forcing a hot/cold tiering or an ANN index?
- **Current-tech hook:** sqlite-vec is brute-force/full-scan only (no HNSW/IVF yet, stable-release blog); fine to 'hundreds of thousands' then linear. Native appendNativePayload (ContentView.swift:2327) is append-only NDJSON. Founder's never-delete principle (trace-perfect-recall-decision) removes the natural eviction valve.

### thermal-8 — ANE contention — OCR, ASR, embeddings, detector and VLM all want the same Neural Engine ⚠️
- **Why:** The scan's good news ('everything except the VLM is real-time on-device') quietly assumes each runs ALONE. WhisperKit, Vision OCR, MiniLM-CoreML, YOLO, and FastVLM's vision encoder are ALL ANE-targeted. The ANE is a single shared accelerator; concurrent models serialize or fall back to GPU/CPU (hotter, slower). The per-helper latencies (OCR 0.31s, ASR 0.46s) were measured in isolation, not contending.
- **Failure if ignored:** Real concurrent latency is far worse than the sum of published solo numbers because ANE requests queue; some helpers spill to GPU/CPU raising power and heat; live-path latency budget blown. The architecture looks feasible on a spec sheet (each block real-time) but the SHARED accelerator is the true bottleneck nobody priced in.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Running OCR + ASR + embeddings + detector + periodic VLM concurrently on the same device, what is each channel's measured latency and ANE utilization vs. its solo number, and how much load spills to GPU/CPU (and adds heat) under contention?
- **Current-tech hook:** Apple Vision 0.31s, WhisperKit 0.46s, MiniLM low-tens-of-ms — all published SOLO and all ANE-resident. iOS gives no per-process ANE reservation; concurrent CoreML requests serialize on the single ANE. Repo runs these as independent engines (TraceLiveContextEngines.swift) with no accelerator-arbitration.

### thermal-9 — Live web-expansion (INJECTION) energy + the radio tail, not just privacy ⚠️
- **Why:** The single most novel thesis layer (expand a phone number/sign/logo via web lookup) is currently absent, and when added it introduces a NEW power axis other lenses miss: cellular/Wi-Fi radio energy. The LTE/5G radio has a long 'tail' (stays in high-power RRC-connected state ~10s+ after a request). A continuous engine firing frequent small enrichment lookups keeps the radio hot continuously — often more battery than the compute it enriches.
- **Failure if ignored:** Each tiny Brave/Wikidata lookup wakes the radio and holds it in high-power state; ambient continuous enrichment = continuously-hot radio = battery destroyed independently of all the on-device thermal work. The team optimizes ANE compute to the milliwatt while the radio quietly burns the budget.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the per-enrichment radio energy (including RRC tail) on cellular vs Wi-Fi, and what is the max sustainable enrichment-lookup rate before radio energy dominates total draw — forcing batching/coalescing of lookups and an offline Wikidata snapshot for the common cases?
- **Current-tech hook:** Brave API 95% <1s but every query leaves the device; cellular RRC connected-state tail keeps the modem in high power ~seconds after each small request. Repo has ZERO network-enrichment code today (grep-confirmed), so this cost is entirely unbudgeted and must be designed in with batching + local Wikidata snapshot.

### thermal-10 — Capture FPS vs. sharp-frame selection — paying to throw frames away ⚠️
- **Why:** Continuous camera at 30/60fps is a large fixed power draw BEFORE any perception. The repo already gates on sharp/keyframes (CODEX_BRIEF_13 pose+sharp frames), but the camera ISP/sensor cost is incurred regardless of how few frames you actually process. The real lever is capture frame rate and resolution, not just downstream selection — running the sensor hot to discard 95% of frames is wasted watts.
- **Failure if ignored:** Engineering effort goes into smart keyframe selection downstream while the camera sensor + ISP run flat-out upstream, so the biggest fixed power cost is never touched; the device is warm even when the perception pipeline is idle between keyframes.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the standalone power cost of the camera capture session at candidate FPS/resolutions (e.g. 30fps 1080p vs 5fps 720p vs on-demand single-shot), and can capture be driven at the keyframe rate rather than full video rate to cut the fixed sensor/ISP draw?
- **Current-tech hook:** Apple documents ARKit capture-frame-rate-throttling tied to thermal state; RoomPlan's design pushed NNs to ANE specifically to avoid capture frame drops. Repo CaptureV2.swift + sharp-frame selection (CODEX_BRIEF_13) gate downstream; capture-session FPS/resolution power not characterized.

### thermal-11 — Thermal hysteresis / recovery time — the duty cycle has a slow time-constant ⚠️
- **Why:** Once a phone hits .serious/.critical it doesn't recover instantly when you back off; aluminum-body thermal mass means minutes to cool. A naive controller that scales back at .serious and immediately ramps up at .fair will oscillate (ramp -> overheat -> throttle -> ramp), spending most time in degraded states. The TokenBucket scales instantly with thermalState but doesn't model recovery lag or add hysteresis.
- **Failure if ignored:** Control loop oscillates / limit-cycles around the thermal threshold; user experiences erratic quality (good, bad, good, bad) and the device spends excess time hot, accelerating long-term battery aging. Average delivered perception is worse than a conservative fixed lower rate would give.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the device's thermal recovery time-constant (minutes to drop from .serious to .nominal at rest), and does the governor need hysteresis / a slow ramp so the duty cycle settles instead of oscillating? Measure delivered enrichment-per-hour under a real heat cycle vs. the theoretical ceiling.
- **Current-tech hook:** TokenBucket.applyThermalState (EnrichmentScheduler.swift:111) maps state->scale instantly with no hysteresis or recovery model. iPhone thermal mass gives multi-minute cool-down; ARKit throttling onset ~1min shows the heat-up side is fast, cool-down is slow — asymmetric.

### thermal-12 — Low Power Mode and OS-level resource demotion override the whole budget ⚠️
- **Why:** When the user enables Low Power Mode (or the OS auto-enables it at 20%), iOS caps CPU/GPU clocks, reduces background activity, and throttles the ANE indirectly — overriding every budget the app computed. A continuous-capture app spends a lot of time at low battery (because it drains fast, thermal-4), so it will frequently run UNDER LPM, which the repo's thermal model doesn't account for at all (it keys only on thermalState, not lowPowerMode).
- **Failure if ignored:** App keeps trying to run its full helper swarm under LPM, fighting the OS clamp: requests queue, latency balloons, iOS may suspend/kill the background app, and the user (already at low battery) sees the memory engine fail exactly when they kept it running longest. Worse, ignoring LPM is a likely App Store rejection / bad-citizen signal.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Under Low Power Mode, what is the actual achievable helper throughput and is the app even permitted to keep capturing in the background, and does the governor have a distinct LPM policy (drop to OCR/ASR-only text core) separate from thermal scaling?
- **Current-tech hook:** iOS Low Power Mode caps CPU/GPU/background and auto-triggers at 20% battery; ProcessInfo.isLowPowerModeEnabled is the signal. Repo keys only on ProcessInfo.thermalState (EnrichmentScheduler.swift:111) — no isLowPowerModeEnabled handling anywhere (grep-confirmed in native).

### thermal-13 — Mac-brain vs phone-helpers split assumes an offload link that costs its own power/latency ⚠️
- **Why:** The honest architecture is live-bounded-helpers (phone) + unbounded-brain (currently Mac/Ollama: gemma3, bge-m3). If the heavy VLM/fusion brain lives off-device, every brain query ships frames/observations over the network — re-introducing the radio-tail energy (thermal-9) AND a latency/availability dependency. If the brain must live ON-device for a true wearable, then the 'unbounded brain' is a fiction constrained by the same 4-5W wall.
- **Failure if ignored:** Either the product secretly depends on a paired Mac / server (not a standalone wearable, and offload power/latency unbudgeted), or the 'unbounded brain' quietly has to run on the same throttled phone and isn't unbounded at all. The architecture's core live/brain split has an unpriced transport and a hidden device-class assumption.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Where does the heavy VLM + INJECTION fusion brain actually run in the shipping product — on-device (then what's its power/thermal share and is it really 'unbounded'?) or offloaded (then what's the per-query transport energy, latency, and offline-availability)?
- **Current-tech hook:** Repo brain = scripts/ask_home.py + Ollama (gemma3:12b/27b, bge-m3) on Mac (live-screen-as-camera, brain :8765); device emits native_context_digest NDJSON. moondream2 4s TTFT / sub-5 tok/s shows on-device heavy VLM is not 'unbounded'; FastVLM weights public but absolutes unmeasured.


## Latency / real-time / backpressure

### latency-1 — Time-to-context vs time-to-answer split (two distinct SLOs) ⚠️
- **Why:** The paradigm's whole claim is that context is understood BEFORE any query. That requires two independent latency budgets: (a) freshness of the ambient context substrate at the instant a question arrives (time-to-context), and (b) the synchronous query->answer turnaround (time-to-answer). The repo conflates them: the brain answer path (ask_home.compose) is a cold synchronous Ollama call with ASSEMBLER_MIN_TIMEOUT=180s, while the 'context' is whatever JSON files happen to be on disk. There is no defined freshness budget for context at query time.
- **Failure if ignored:** Either the context is stale at answer time (you answer about the world 30s ago, breaking the 'understands live' promise), or you pay full perception cost synchronously inside the query and time-to-answer blows past any conversational bar. Without separating the two SLOs you can't even tell which one failed.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** At the moment a query lands, what is the p50/p95 AGE of the newest context fact that feeds the answer, AND what is the p50/p95 query->first-token and query->full-answer wall time, measured separately on the live device path (not the offline brain)?
- **Current-tech hook:** FastVLM TTFT is the gating perception latency but Apple published only relative speedups (85x vs LLaVA-OV) — you must benchmark absolute TTFT on iPhone 16 Pro yourself; OCR (Apple Vision 0.31s / ML Kit 0.05s), SpeechAnalyzer (<0.5s) and MiniLM embeds (tens of ms) are fast enough to keep context fresh, so the VLM is the only channel that can make time-to-context lag.

### latency-2 — Fixed-cadence sampling with no backpressure (open-loop capture)
- **Why:** trace_live_feed.py advances on a fixed wall-clock schedule (next_t += args.every, default 4s) and only sleeps to catch up — it never checks whether the previous frame's VLM perceive() has finished. The gemma3 perceive call can exceed the sample interval (sub-5 tok/s decode), so the loop is open-loop: it assumes perception is faster than cadence and has no mechanism to slow capture when it isn't.
- **Failure if ignored:** When perception falls behind cadence, frames silently queue or the loop drifts — you accumulate an ever-growing backlog of unperceived frames, context age climbs unbounded, and the 'live' read is actually minutes behind reality. No signal tells the system or the user that it's drowning.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Under sustained capture, what is the steady-state gap between frame capture time and frame perceive-completion time, and at what --every value does perceive latency exceed the interval and the backlog begin to grow monotonically?
- **Current-tech hook:** sub-5 tok/s VLM decode means a multi-sentence SCENE/OBJECTS/TEXT/PEOPLE perceive prompt can take several seconds; at --every 4 on a thermally-throttled (4-5W sustained) device the loop will go closed-cadence-violating within the first minute of throttle.

### latency-3 — Queue max-age / staleness eviction is the only backpressure primitive — and it's device-only ⚠️
- **Why:** The native EnrichmentScheduler is the single place in the repo with real backpressure: a per-track queue, staleAfterSeconds=60 eviction, salience-ranked single-item dequeue, and a thermal-scaled TokenBucket. This is good — but it governs only WHICH tracks get a VLM enrichment, not the end-to-end pipeline, and the Mac/brain path (trace_live_feed + ask_home) has NO equivalent: no queue, no max-age, no drop policy.
- **Failure if ignored:** Backpressure that exists only on-device and only for the enrichment sub-stage gives a false sense of safety. The OCR/ASR/fusion/answer stages have no admission control, so a burst (text-dense scene, rapid scene changes) overruns them with no eviction — and the offline brain has unbounded queues that just grow memory.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** For every stage (capture, OCR, VLM, ASR, fusion, answer), what is its max queue depth and max item age before drop, and which stages today have NEITHER — i.e. where can a burst cause unbounded growth?
- **Current-tech hook:** The TokenBucket.applyThermalState (nominal 1.0 -> critical 0.1) is exactly the right primitive and should be generalized: thermal throttle begins ~1 min into sustained capture, so the budget MUST shrink the moment ProcessInfo.thermalState degrades, which the scheduler already does but nothing downstream respects.

### latency-4 — Drop-vs-resume policy and which channel is sacrificed under load ⚠️
- **Why:** Under thermal/CPU pressure something must be dropped. The honesty moat says refusals must NAME the missing channel. That means the drop policy is not just a performance knob — it is a correctness/honesty contract: if the VLM channel is shed under heat, the answer packet must KNOW the VLM was absent for that window so it can refuse 'I wasn't looking closely then' rather than answer from stale data as if fresh.
- **Failure if ignored:** Silent drops violate the honesty moat: a sched/thermal-induced gap in a channel looks identical to 'nothing happened', so the engine confidently answers over a blind spot it doesn't know it had. Priority inversion: a cheap honest channel (OCR) gets starved while an expensive low-value VLM call holds the budget.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** When the budget forces a drop, is the dropped channel + its time-window recorded as an explicit gap observation, and can a query whose answer falls inside that gap detect it and refuse-by-naming the dropped channel? What is the channel priority order under load?
- **Current-tech hook:** Apple Vision OCR confidence values + the existing TEXT:NONE refusal give a model for 'honest absence'; the SchedulerStats (budgetDenied, evictedStale, belowThreshold) already count drops but are not surfaced into the answer packet as gap-provenance.

### latency-5 — Injection-layer web-expansion latency is on the synchronous answer path and externally variable ⚠️
- **Why:** The thesis' novel layer (EXPAND a phone number -> institution via web/knowledge lookup) is network I/O that does not exist yet. If implemented naively it sits inline before phrasing, adding Brave's '95% < 1s' BUT 5% tail (and DNS/TLS/retry) to every enriched answer — and unlike on-device stages its latency is unbounded by anything you control. It also tail-couples answer latency to connectivity.
- **Failure if ignored:** A single slow/failed enrichment lookup stalls the whole answer (head-of-line blocking), or you set a tight timeout and silently answer without the expansion — producing a less-grounded answer with no signal that expansion was skipped. Offline => every answer pays a full timeout before falling back.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the per-enrichment lookup p50/p95/p99 latency and timeout, is expansion on the synchronous answer path or precomputed/cached, and what does the answer do (refuse? answer-degraded-and-say-so?) when the lookup times out or the device is offline?
- **Current-tech hook:** Brave Search API 95%<1s but metered ($5/1k) and network-bound; a local Wikidata/Wikipedia snapshot answers the common expansions in-memory (sub-ms) and keeps the privacy + latency story intact — live Brave only for cache misses, behind a hard timeout.

### latency-6 — Assembler double-pass grounding gate doubles answer latency ⚠️
- **Why:** answer_assembler runs think_and_answer then, when ASSEMBLER_GROUNDING_GATE is on, a second verification pass at ~2x latency (the code comment says exactly this), plus verify_grounded is itself another full _ollama call. On a sub-5 tok/s local model with ASSEMBLER_MIN_TIMEOUT floored at 180s, the honesty machinery is the dominant latency cost, not perception.
- **Failure if ignored:** The product's differentiator (honest grounding) makes it too slow to feel 'live/ambient'; users perceive a multi-second-to-minutes lag on every answer. If you cut the gate to hit a latency bar you trade away the honesty moat — the two are in direct tension and nobody has measured the exchange rate.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the added wall-clock of each honesty pass (structural_grounding, verify_grounded, the assembler 2x gate) as a fraction of total answer latency, and what is the accuracy/latency Pareto curve as you disable each pass?
- **Current-tech hook:** MLX-VLM ~2x tok/s over GGUF on identical hardware and FastVLM-0.5B fast TTFT could fund the second pass within budget; but on the current Ollama/gemma3 path the 180s floor shows the gate is already the bottleneck.

### latency-7 — Consensus window requires N temporally-adjacent frames — a latency-to-confidence floor ⚠️
- **Why:** consensus_read votes across a +-half-second window of frames with minrep>=2 agreement before it will assert. Confidence is therefore a FUNCTION OF DWELL TIME: you physically cannot have a high-confidence read until enough frames covering the same text have accrued. This couples answer confidence to how long the user lingered — a real-time hard floor that no amount of compute removes.
- **Failure if ignored:** Ask immediately after glancing at a sign and the window is empty/below-quorum, so the honest engine refuses (NOT IN MEMORY) — correct but feels broken ('I just showed it the sign!'). Tune the window down for responsiveness and hallucination returns. The dwell->confidence latency is invisible to the user.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the minimum dwell time (seconds of frames on the same text) to reach minrep>=2 quorum at the live sampling cadence, and what fraction of real glance-and-ask interactions fall below that floor and thus must refuse?
- **Current-tech hook:** The native EnrichmentScheduler already encodes dwell as the salience driver (8s/24s/72s ladder); aligning the consensus window to the same dwell accounting, and surfacing 'still gathering' as a distinct state from 'not in memory', is the honest fix.

### latency-8 — Clock-domain skew across helpers breaks temporal fusion and anchoring ⚠️
- **Why:** Fusion, consensus windows, and the anchored read path all key on timestamps (center=float(anchor), +-half second windows, source+timestamp tags). But helpers run on different clocks/cadences: device CoreLocation geocode, on-device Speech committed-segment latency, whisper streaming lag, VLM perceive completion time vs frame capture time, and offline-built audio_events. If their timestamps aren't aligned to a single capture-time base, the consensus window pulls in the wrong frames.
- **Failure if ignored:** OCR from t=80.0s gets fused with speech that was actually SPOKEN at 80.0 but COMMITTED at 81.5 and stamped 81.5 — so cross-helper corroboration silently misaligns, the +-0.5s window misses true matches and catches false ones, and the anchored read centers on the wrong moment. Subtle, data-dependent, and invisible in aggregate metrics.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the timestamp-skew (capture-time vs emit-time) per helper, is every observation stamped with a single common capture clock, and how wide must the consensus window be to absorb worst-case skew without pulling in unrelated frames?
- **Current-tech hook:** WhisperKit streaming ~0.46s mean latency and Speech committed-segment delay mean ASR emit-time trails audio-time by hundreds of ms; ARKit/AVFoundation give a presentation timestamp per frame that should be the single authoritative clock all helpers stamp against.

### latency-9 — Cold-start / model-load latency on the first query after idle ⚠️
- **Why:** Ambient engines idle for long stretches then must answer instantly. Ollama/gemma3 (and a Core ML FastVLM/MiniLM stack) pay model load + ANE compile + first-inference warmup on the first call after eviction. The repo's synchronous _ollama call has no warmth guarantee; the first answer after the OS reclaims memory pays the full cold cost on top of the 180s-floored timeout.
- **Failure if ignored:** The very first question of a session — the one that forms the user's impression — is the slowest, exhibiting multi-second-to-tens-of-seconds cold latency, then it 'mysteriously' speeds up. Looks like a flaky product; actually deterministic cold start.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the delta between cold-start and warm answer latency for each model (VLM, embedder, gate LLM), how long until the OS evicts a warm model under memory pressure, and is a keep-warm/duty-cycle heartbeat needed?
- **Current-tech hook:** 32GB serialize pressure (noted in the live-feed memory) and iPhone memory reclaim make eviction likely; Core ML ANE first-compile and Ollama keep_alive are the concrete knobs — a low-rate keep-warm ping trades idle power for predictable first-answer latency.

### latency-10 — Jitter / variance, not mean, governs perceived 'ambient liveness' ⚠️
- **Why:** An ambient assistant is judged by worst-case responsiveness and consistency, not average. The pipeline's latency variance is huge: data-dependent VLM token counts, thermal-state transitions (nominal->serious halves budget mid-session), network enrichment tails, cold/warm splits, and consensus-quorum-or-refuse branching. Mean latency hides all of it.
- **Failure if ignored:** Optimizing/reporting on mean latency (the founder's instinct) masks a fat tail where 1-in-20 answers take 10x longer or thermal throttle suddenly degrades everything after minute one. Users remember the jitter, not the mean; the demo (cool device, short) never shows it.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What are p95/p99 and the full latency distribution (not mean) for time-to-answer across a SUSTAINED 10-minute session that crosses a thermal-state transition, and how much does p99 degrade once throttling begins?
- **Current-tech hook:** A18 Pro throttles from 8-10W peak to ~4-5W sustained starting ~1 min in — a deterministic mid-session latency cliff; benchmarking must run past the throttle point, not the 30s demo window, to capture the real p99.

### latency-11 — Salience/budget scheduler can starve a low-salience-but-queried entity (priority inversion) ⚠️
- **Why:** EnrichmentScheduler dequeues max-salience first and evicts stale tracks at 60s; salience = dwell*(novelty,stability). A thing the user will ASK about is not necessarily high-salience to the scorer (it may be static, familiar, low-motion). The scheduler's priority is set by perceptual salience, not by future query relevance, so the exact entity the user cares about can be perpetually out-budgeted or evicted before it's enriched.
- **Failure if ignored:** Priority inversion: high-novelty background churn consumes the VLM budget while the static document the user is reading never clears threshold, so when they ask about it the engine has no enrichment and must refuse. The system was busy — on the wrong things.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** For entities that users actually query, what fraction were below the salience threshold or evicted-stale before enrichment, and does query history need to feed back into salience to prevent starving askable-but-boring entities?
- **Current-tech hook:** Familiarity-down-weighting (novelty term) actively penalizes the stable text/document case that OCR+consensus is BEST at; the scheduler's threshold=0.45 and staleAfterSeconds=60 are the two knobs that decide whether the product's strongest channel even gets fed.

### latency-12 — No end-to-end latency deadline / admission control — only per-call timeouts ⚠️
- **Why:** Every stage has its own timeout (Ollama timeout, ASSEMBLER_MIN_TIMEOUT=180), but there is no global query deadline that bounds the SUM across consensus + fusion + expansion + draft + verify + gate. Latencies compose additively; a query can legitimately stack multiple 180s-floored passes. Nothing says 'this answer must be done in N seconds or degrade.'
- **Failure if ignored:** Worst-case end-to-end latency is the SUM of every stage's worst case (cold VLM + slow consensus + network enrichment tail + double-pass gate) with no ceiling — an answer can take minutes, and there's no graceful-degradation path that returns a best-effort grounded answer at the deadline instead of running to completion.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the measured worst-case sum-of-stages end-to-end latency for a fully-enriched answer, and is there a deadline-driven degradation ladder (drop expansion -> drop second gate pass -> answer-with-current-evidence) that guarantees an answer within a fixed budget?
- **Current-tech hook:** The TokenBucket model generalizes to a per-query latency budget that's spent across stages; a deadline scheduler (answer with whatever evidence is fused when the clock expires, naming what was skipped) preserves both the latency bound and the honesty moat.

### latency-13 — Consensus recall is currently a side-path, not the default — fusion latency is unbudgeted where it runs ⚠️
- **Why:** consensus_read fires only on the anchored reading/screen path (anchor is not None); the default assembler is per-channel ranked concatenation. The thesis wants consensus as the DEFAULT fusion mechanic across all channels. Moving it there multiplies its windowing/clustering cost across every channel and every query — a latency change nobody has costed because it's never run in the hot path.
- **Failure if ignored:** Promoting consensus to the default fusion stage (as the blueprint demands) silently adds per-channel windowing + substring-clustering cost to every answer; if it's O(frames^2) per channel it could dominate fusion latency and push time-to-answer past budget exactly when you scale to a real day's memory.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is consensus_read's latency as a function of window size and frames-in-window, and what does making it the default cross-channel fusion mechanic add to per-query fusion latency at realistic memory sizes (a full day of keyframes)?
- **Current-tech hook:** consensus_read does NO extra LLM calls (it clusters cached OCR strings) so it's CPU-cheap relative to the VLM, which is the argument for promoting it — but substring-cluster cost over ASSEMBLER_MAX_PER_CHANNEL*channels frames at day-scale must be measured, not assumed cheap.

### latency-14 — Write-path contention: continuous capture writing JSON memory vs query read-path ⚠️
- **Why:** Helpers continuously append to kf_memory.json / world_memory.json / transcript etc. while a query simultaneously reads/resolves them (_resolve_memories). Plain JSON files have no concurrent-read-during-write story; a query landing mid-flush either reads a partial/locked file or blocks. As capture rate and memory size grow, write amplification (rewriting whole JSON blobs) competes with read latency.
- **Failure if ignored:** A query during an active capture flush stalls or reads a truncated/inconsistent memory file, intermittently spiking answer latency or corrupting the evidence packet; whole-file JSON rewrites turn O(1) appends into O(memory-size) writes that lengthen the write window and the contention window with it.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the read-path latency of a query issued DURING a capture write, how does it scale with memory-file size over a multi-hour session, and at what size does whole-file JSON rewrite latency start blocking queries?
- **Current-tech hook:** sqlite-vec + SQLCipher with WAL (the recommended store) gives concurrent reader-during-writer with bounded append latency — exactly the fix for plain-JSON whole-file rewrite contention; migrating the hot kf/world/transcript files off JSON onto WAL'd SQLite removes this contention class entirely.


## Continuous attention / salience — what deserves expensive compute now

### attention-1 — Salience-blind sampling on the live path (fixed-clock vs attention-driven) ⚠️
- **Why:** The shippable live spine (scripts/trace_live_feed.py) samples on a dumb wall clock — `--every 4.0s`, time.sleep loop at :260-265. It captures whether or not anything salient is happening. The sophisticated salience ladder (EnrichmentScheduler.swift) lives ONLY in the native app and is never invoked on the Mac live path. So the actual running engine spends equal compute on a blank wall and on a dense bilingual departure board.
- **Failure if ignored:** Two simultaneous failures: misses fast events between 4s ticks (a sign glanced for 2s never gets a frame), AND wastes the scarce ~4-5W thermal budget perceiving static/empty scenes — which on a phone means you throttle in ~1 min having learned nothing. The consensus-recall win depends on capturing the SAME text across neighbouring frames; a fixed 4s clock on a moving camera may never put the same sign in two frames.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On the Munich walk capture, what fraction of fixed-4s frames carried zero new salient content (no new OCR token, no new track), and what fraction of distinct readable signs appeared in <2 frames (i.e. below consensus quorum)? Quantify the compute wasted and the recall lost vs an adaptive sampler.
- **Current-tech hook:** ML Kit OCR at 0.05s/frame and a CoreML MiniLM embed at low-tens-of-ms are cheap enough to run as a CHEAP GATE on every frame at 10-30fps, and trigger the expensive VLM only on novelty. The thermal data (throttle in ~1min at sustained load) makes adaptive duty-cycling mandatory, not optional.

### attention-2 — Salience score has no speech-reference / deictic term ⚠️
- **Why:** SalienceScorer.score (EnrichmentScheduler.swift:64) = dwell × (0.6·novelty + 0.4·stability). It is purely vision-internal. Nothing routes 'the user just said this/that/look at — point compute HERE NOW'. On-device Apple Speech is live (TraceLiveContextEngines.swift, requiresOnDeviceRecognition=true) but its transcript is never coupled back into the attention budget. A deictic utterance is the single strongest natural salience signal a wearable gets, and it's discarded.
- **Failure if ignored:** User says 'what does that sign say?' and the engine, mid-dwell on an unrelated person track, spends its budget token elsewhere and refuses the very thing the user pointed at. The product feels deaf — it perceives ambiently but cannot be DIRECTED, which is the whole promise of [Context→Prompt→Answer].
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** When does a speech reference ('this', 'that', 'look', a named object) arrive relative to the relevant frame, and can a deixis term added to the salience score raise the right track above threshold (0.45) within one budget refill? Measure: median latency from deictic utterance to a VLM pass on the referent track.
- **Current-tech hook:** WhisperKit / SpeechAnalyzer deliver committed segments at <0.5s on-device — fast enough that a deictic word can boost a track's salience inside the same dwell window. The hook already half-exists: speech is captured; it just needs to feed score().

### attention-3 — Hand/interaction cues are detected but never raise salience ⚠️
- **Why:** self_entity.py:65 already regexes a rich interaction vocabulary (hands holding/gripping/reaching/pointing/pushing/zipping/tying/rummaging/packing). This is the strongest 'what matters to the user right now' signal short of gaze — humans attend to what their hands touch. But it is consumed only for first-person identity binding, NOT fed into the salience/budget decision. Object-being-manipulated should be the highest-priority enrichment target and currently isn't.
- **Failure if ignored:** User picks up a medication box / business card / boarding pass and inspects it — the precise moment maximal recall value exists — and the scheduler treats that object identically to background clutter, possibly never spending a token on it before it leaves frame.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** In the capture corpus, how often does a hand-interaction cue co-occur with an object that the user later asks about? If interaction-boosted salience were added, what is the precision/recall lift on 'what did I just pick up / read' questions vs the dwell-only scorer?
- **Current-tech hook:** On-device hand-pose / VNDetectHumanHandPose ships in Vision today and runs on ANE cheaply; pairing a hand bbox with a detector track is a near-term build, not aspirational.

### attention-4 — Dwell measures time-in-view, not confirmed attention (camera ≠ gaze) ⚠️
- **Why:** temporal_specialist.py:17,273 explicitly disclaims this: stored dwell is time-in-FRAME, not confirmed attention/dwell time. On a chest/phone-mounted camera the field of view is whatever the body points at, which is NOT where the eyes are. The salience ladder escalates knowledge depth by dwell (8s/24s/72s) — escalating compute on whatever happens to sit in frame longest, e.g. the user's own lap or a wall, not what they're actually looking at.
- **Failure if ignored:** Compute escalation rewards stationary background (a wall in frame for 72s gets minutiae-level VLM passes) while a glanced-at fixated object (2s) never escalates past overview. Budget burns on the boring stable thing precisely because stability and dwell are both rewarded.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the correlation between in-frame dwell and what the user actually asks about later? Concretely: of objects that earned level-3 (minutiae) enrichment by dwell, what fraction were ever queried — vs the query rate of objects that left frame quickly?
- **Current-tech hook:** True gaze needs eye-tracking hardware absent on iPhone; the honest near-term proxy is frame-center weighting + optical-flow stabilization (camera fixation), and motion (already in scorer as `stability`) — but center-bias must be ADDED so 'what's centered' beats 'what's been parked in the corner longest'.

### attention-5 — Thermal token bucket is the real attention budget — and its calibration is unvalidated ⚠️
- **Why:** TokenBucket.applyThermalState (EnrichmentScheduler.swift:111) maps nominal/fair/serious/critical → 1.0/0.7/0.4/0.1 scale on a base of 30 enrichments/hour (EnrichmentGovernor.shared = perHour:30). This single mapping silently decides how much the product can ever perceive. 30/hour = one VLM pass every 2 minutes at nominal — but the current-tech scan says the phone throttles in ~1 MINUTE of sustained VLM. So the budget may be set for a thermal reality that doesn't exist, and the scale factors are guesses with no measured throttle curve behind them.
- **Failure if ignored:** Either too generous (engine commits 30 VLM passes/hr the SoC can't sustain → throttle → frame drops → the very capture that fuels consensus-recall collapses), or too conservative (refuses to look when it safely could). Worse: thermalState is a coarse 4-level signal that lags actual die temp, so by the time it reads .serious you're already throttling.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On the target device under continuous capture, what is the measured wall-clock time-to-throttle at 30/hr, at 60/hr, at the duty-cycle that holds nominal indefinitely? Derive the actual sustainable enrichments/hour and replace the guessed 30 with it.
- **Current-tech hook:** A18 Pro: 8-10W peak, ~4-5W sustained, throttle onset ~1min (Apple ARKit throttling docs). ProcessInfo.thermalState + a power-budget sampler can calibrate the real curve; FastVLM-0.5B's fast TTFT is the lever for fitting more passes per watt.

### attention-6 — No cheap pre-gate before the expensive VLM pass (gate cost vs payload cost)
- **Why:** The architecture is helpers→injection→LLM, but on the live path every selected frame goes straight to the gemma3 VLM (trace_live_feed.py perceive). There is no cheap front gate (is this frame even worth a VLM call?) — OCR and detector run, but they're not used to SUPPRESS a VLM call on a redundant/blank frame. The whole point of a salience layer is that the gate must be orders of magnitude cheaper than the thing it gates; here the gate and the payload are conflated.
- **Failure if ignored:** VLM (the one sub-5-tok/s, thermally expensive component) fires on frames a 0.05s OCR pass could have shown were identical to the last one. You pay the most expensive operation to learn 'nothing changed' — the worst possible compute allocation on a thermally capped device.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the per-frame cost ratio gate:payload (OCR+detector+embed-delta vs one VLM pass) on-device, and what fraction of VLM calls would a 'frame-delta below epsilon → skip VLM' gate eliminate on the walk corpus without losing any queried content?
- **Current-tech hook:** MiniLM-CoreML embedding delta + ML Kit OCR token-set delta = a <50ms gate; FastVLM TTFT (Apple hides absolutes, sub-5 tok/s decode) = the expensive payload. The ratio is plausibly 10-100×, which is exactly the regime where gating pays.

### attention-7 — Novelty is per-label familiarity, not per-instance / per-content novelty ⚠️
- **Why:** SalienceScorer novelty (EnrichmentScheduler.swift:68) = 1 − familiarity(className), where familiarity = min(1, labelEnriched[label]/3). After a label ('sign', 'person', 'screen') has been enriched 3 times, ALL future instances of that class read as zero-novelty. But the product's whole value is reading the 50th DIFFERENT sign, the 50th different screen of text. Class-level habituation actively suppresses the thing that matters most: a new instance of a familiar category.
- **Failure if ignored:** Walk past 3 signs early; every subsequent sign — including the one with the gate number you need — scores novelty 0 and never earns a VLM pass. The engine 'gets bored' of the category that is its core product (text-bearing surfaces) after three exposures.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** If novelty were computed on CONTENT (OCR token-set / embedding distance from prior reads) instead of class label, how many additional distinct signs/screens cross threshold on the walk corpus, and does query-answerability rise?
- **Current-tech hook:** Per-instance content novelty is computable today: hash/embed the OCR text (MiniLM-CoreML) and measure cosine distance to the running store (sqlite-vec). Cheap, on-device, and turns 'have I seen this CLASS' into 'have I seen this CONTENT'.

### attention-8 — Absence>60s hard-resets dwell — fixation continuity across glances is lost ⚠️
- **Why:** EnrichmentGovernor.tick (EnrichmentScheduler.swift:258) resets firstSeen if a label was unseen >60s: 'reappearance is a new fixation'. But real attention is interrupted glances — you look at a menu, away to the waiter, back to the menu. A 60s binary reset means the second glance starts dwell from zero and may never re-escalate, while two 50s-apart glances are treated as one continuous 100s+ dwell. The continuity model is a crude single threshold.
- **Failure if ignored:** Repeated short returns to the same object (classic real-world attention pattern) never accumulate enough continuous dwell to earn deep enrichment, so the object the user keeps coming back to — the strongest implicit salience signal there is — stays at overview depth.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the real-world distribution of glance-away gaps for objects users repeatedly attend to? Is a single 60s reset right, or does cumulative/decaying dwell (sum of glances with a forgetting factor) better predict what gets queried?
- **Current-tech hook:** Track re-identification across gaps is the dependency (the comment admits 'person identity is the session-singleton simplification'); lightweight on-device re-ID / appearance embeddings make decaying-dwell feasible without raw-media retention.

### attention-9 — Single global budget — no priority lanes for honest-refusal-critical vs ambient content ⚠️
- **Why:** One TokenBucket governs all enrichment (EnrichmentGovernor.shared). There is no reserved lane for the queries the honesty moat depends on. When the user asks a question that needs a verbatim read (a clock time, a gate number) and the structural gate (ask_home G2) will REFUSE unless the value literally appears in the corpus, that read is competing for the same scarce token as background ambient curiosity — and may lose, forcing an honest-but-useless refusal.
- **Failure if ignored:** The product refuses a perfectly answerable question ('it left frame before I could read it') not because the content wasn't there but because the budget allocator spent the token on ambient noise. Honesty becomes an excuse for an attention-allocation bug. Refusal rate gets coupled to budget contention, not to ground truth.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Should there be a reserved high-priority budget lane triggered by an active user query / deictic reference? Measure: what fraction of GROUNDED_REFUSALs on answerable questions are actually budget-starvation (the content existed in a frame that was sampled but never VLM-enriched)?
- **Current-tech hook:** A two-bucket scheme (ambient lane + query-reserved lane) is trivial on the existing TokenBucket; the trigger signal (active query) already exists at the ask_home seam. FastVLM-0.5B's fast TTFT makes an on-demand priority pass viable within an interaction's patience window.

### attention-10 — Salience↔consensus coupling — adaptive sampling can starve the frequency=confidence mechanic ⚠️
- **Why:** consensus_recall.py needs the SAME text in MULTIPLE neighbouring frames (frequency = vote weight, quorum to refuse). But any salience/novelty-driven sampler is biased AGAINST capturing the same content twice (novelty suppresses repeats — see attention-7). So the two load-bearing mechanisms are in direct tension: the attention layer wants to STOP looking at what it's seen, the honesty layer needs to look at it AGAIN to confirm. Nobody has reconciled these.
- **Failure if ignored:** Make sampling more efficient (skip redundant frames) and you destroy consensus quorum → reads drop below vote threshold → refuse content you actually saw clearly. Optimizing the attention lens silently regresses the validated 47%→60% text-recall win.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the minimum re-capture count per sign needed to hold consensus quorum, and can a salience sampler be made consensus-aware (deliberately re-sample a high-value text region N times before habituating) without blowing the thermal budget? Measure recall vs frames-per-sign tradeoff.
- **Current-tech hook:** Cheap OCR (ML Kit 0.05s) means re-reading the same region N times is nearly free relative to a VLM pass — so consensus can be served by cheap repeated OCR while novelty habituation governs only the expensive VLM lane. The two lanes can be decoupled by cost tier.

### attention-11 — Motion term is dual-purpose and possibly inverted for text capture ⚠️
- **Why:** stability = 1 − motion (EnrichmentScheduler.swift:69) rewards static subjects — correct for avoiding motion-blurred VLM passes. But on a walking user, EVERYTHING the camera sees is in relative motion; the signal that a readable sign exists often co-occurs with the user STOPPING to read it (low motion) OR with brief settle frames. A single scalar motion penalty can't distinguish 'blurry, skip' from 'user paused to read, capture NOW'.
- **Failure if ignored:** Walking past signage = high motion = low stability = low salience = no enrichment, exactly when the text is most fleeting and most needs a fast grab. The product underperforms in its core scenario (reading the world while moving) because motion is treated as pure noise.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Does a sharpness/blur metric (Laplacian variance) per-frame outperform the track-level motion scalar at predicting which frames yield clean OCR? Measure OCR-yield as a function of motion vs sharpness, and whether 'user paused' (motion derivative → 0) is a better capture trigger than absolute low motion.
- **Current-tech hook:** Per-frame Laplacian-variance sharpness gating is the proven trick (already referenced in CODEX_BRIEF_13_pose_sharp_frames); it runs in microseconds on-device and is a better grab-trigger than the coarse motion scalar.

### attention-12 — No interrupt / barge-in path — perception cannot be preempted by a live event ⚠️
- **Why:** The scheduler is poll-based: host calls observe() then nextEnrichment() per tick; salience is recomputed each tick but there is no preemption — an in-flight VLM pass (multi-second on-device) cannot be cancelled when something far more salient appears (user speaks, hand grabs an object, a critical sign flashes). On a sub-5-tok/s VLM, a single pass blocks the budget for seconds.
- **Failure if ignored:** A VLM pass on a low-value background person is in flight when the user picks up and reads a document; the high-value event must wait seconds for the budget/compute to free, and the document is gone by then. The system can't 'snap to' what suddenly matters.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the on-device VLM pass duration (TTFT + decode) for FastVLM-0.5B, and over that window how often does a higher-salience event arrive that would justify preemption? Quantify the missed-event rate caused by non-preemptible passes.
- **Current-tech hook:** FastVLM's design goal is fast TTFT specifically to shorten this blocking window; pairing short-output 'overview' passes (low token count) on the live lane with cancellable async 'minutiae' passes on the brain lane is the shippable mitigation.

### attention-13 — Two divergent salience implementations that must stay in sync (Swift + Python) ⚠️
- **Why:** EnrichmentScheduler.swift header (:2-4) declares it a '1:1 port of trace_perception/scheduler.py' whose contract is tests/test_enrichment_scheduler.py, and 'any behavior change must land in BOTH'. Salience tuning (thresholds, weights, the 0.6/0.4 split, dwell ladder) is the most empirically-tuned part of an attention engine — and it lives in two hand-synced copies. Drift here silently changes WHAT THE PRODUCT PAYS ATTENTION TO, differently on Mac vs device.
- **Failure if ignored:** A weight tuned on the Mac eval (Python) doesn't make it into Swift; the device pays attention to different things than the eval measured; the validated numbers don't hold on the actual product. Worst kind of bug: invisible, and it invalidates the eval.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Are the two implementations currently in sync (does test_enrichment_scheduler.py pass against BOTH), and what is the cost of replacing the dual-impl with a single shared core (e.g. a tiny portable spec or shared library) before any further salience tuning?
- **Current-tech hook:** The contract-test approach is right but fragile; a single source (compile the scorer once, or a golden-vector conformance suite run against both) is the standard fix and cheap to add now while the scorer is still small.

### attention-14 — No salience signal for text-density / read-value — the product's core target isn't a first-class salience input ⚠️
- **Why:** The pivot is 'a memory for everything you READ'. Yet salience is scored on detector tracks (person/object classes) with seen_count>=3 (TraceDetectorBridge.swift:212) — generic object detection, NOT a text-presence channel. OCR runs (in-memory, authoritative) but OCR token-density does not feed the salience/budget decision. The engine allocates expensive attention by object class, while the thing it's supposed to remember (dense readable text) has no seat at the salience table.
- **Failure if ignored:** A wall of departure-board text scores no higher for enrichment than a blank chair, because neither is a high-salience detector class. The product is structurally blind to its own value signal at the moment of attention allocation — it reads text by luck of the 4s clock, not by deciding text is worth looking at.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** If OCR token-count / text-region area per frame were added as a salience term, how much does it raise the capture rate of the signs/screens users actually query, and does it let the engine spend its budget preferentially on text-rich frames?
- **Current-tech hook:** ML Kit / Apple Vision already return text bounding boxes and per-word confidence cheaply (0.05–0.31s); text-region area and word-count are free byproducts that can directly weight salience — a same-day wiring change, not new ML.


## Helper taxonomy / diversity

### helpers-1 — Monolithic VLM masquerading as a society of specialists ⚠️
- **Why:** The thesis demands many diverse parallel helpers, none authoritative. But scripts/trace_live_feed.py:40 PERCEIVE_PROMPT is ONE prompt asking ONE gemma3 model for SCENE+OBJECTS+TEXT+PEOPLE in a single forward pass. That is a single captioner wearing four hats, not four independent perceivers. A single model's hallucination contaminates all four channels at once (correlated failure), and they cannot disagree to drive corroboration — defeating the frequency=confidence honesty mechanic the whole design rests on.
- **Failure if ignored:** Apparent diversity is fake; when gemma3 invents a 'PEOPLE: 2 waiting' it also drifts SCENE/OBJECTS coherently with the lie, so cross-channel corroboration sees agreement and rubber-stamps the fabrication. The honesty moat silently inverts: redundancy that should catch lies instead launders one model's single hallucination into four 'independent' votes.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** If you split the monolithic prompt into N truly independent perceivers (separate model calls or separate models per aspect), what fraction of fabrications that survive today get caught by genuine inter-helper disagreement — and what is the per-frame latency/thermal cost of N forward passes vs 1 under the ~4-5W sustained envelope?
- **Current-tech hook:** FastVLM-0.5B's 85x faster TTFT makes per-aspect specialist calls newly affordable on key frames; ML Kit OCR (0.05s) and WhisperKit are ALREADY separate models, proving the heterogeneous-specialist path works — the VLM is the one channel still collapsed into a monolith.

### helpers-2 — Open-vocab vs typed-slot coverage cliff ⚠️
- **Why:** structured_recall.py only has hand-coded slots: wearer_identity/outfit/institution/labeled_examples/occupancy/display-count (classify_slot:88). These are the ONLY fact types that get frequency-corroboration into typed facts; everything else falls back to the flattened, vote-less dossier. The helper taxonomy is therefore bimodal: a tiny set of high-trust typed facts and a vast open-vocab tail with no corroboration. Any entity the founder didn't pre-enumerate (a price, a departure time, a dosage, a wifi password) lives in the untyped, fabrication-prone tier.
- **Failure if ignored:** The product is honest exactly on the six things someone hard-coded and quietly fabrication-prone on everything else. As real-world capture broadens, the share of questions hitting the un-typed tail grows, so measured honesty on a 15-Q eval (which happens to hit the typed slots) collapses on a real n.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On a held-out text-rich capture, what fraction of answerable questions resolve to a hand-coded structured slot vs the un-corroborated open-vocab dossier, and what is the honesty delta between those two populations?
- **Current-tech hook:** On-device MiniLM-CoreML embeddings (low-tens-of-ms) make open-vocab clustering of arbitrary observed strings feasible without enumerating slots — frequency-consensus could run over ANY repeated token, not just six pre-named categories.

### helpers-3 — Missing helper MODALITIES (the taxonomy holes) ⚠️
- **Why:** Through the diversity lens the live set is: VLM-caption, OCR, ASR, GPS, detector+salience, capture-time audio-events. Entire perception classes that a 'memory for everything you read/encounter' needs are absent: no barcode/QR decoder, no face/person re-identification across frames (only detector seen_count, no identity persistence), no logo/brand recognizer, no document-layout/structure parser, no color/material primitive as its OWN channel (it's buried in the VLM caption), no motion/gesture/activity recognizer, no depth/spatial-geometry helper, no time/clock reader as a typed channel. Each absent type is a class of questions that can only be answered by the hallucination-prone VLM.
