- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the duty-cycle coordination policy: given device thermalState/battery (already in packet metadata) and Mac availability, who runs the heavy pass and when? Measure: under sustained capture, device time-to-throttle (the ~1min wall) and whether offloading the heavy pass to the Mac extends sustainable capture duration.
- **Current-tech hook:** A18 Pro ~1min-to-throttle / 4-5W sustained makes on-device heavy VLM thermally impossible — so the heavy pass MUST be opportunistically offloaded to the Mac/cloud when reachable, and the device must downgrade to cheap-helpers-only when not. The scheduler already reads ProcessInfo.thermalState (:254); the topology must let that signal gate WHERE work runs, not just whether.

### topology-11 — Hub address is hand-typed and historically comma-bugged — discovery/binding is fragile ⚠️
- **Why:** The device finds the Mac via a manually entered IP (ContentView.swift:2553 hubURL from typed string; the code carries scar tissue for 'the historic comma-bug class' :2420 where a bad URL silently spooled every packet). There is no service discovery (Bonjour/mDNS). DEFAULT is 127.0.0.1:8765 (:2404) which is meaningless from a separate physical device.
- **Failure if ignored:** On a new network, or after a DHCP lease change, the device's hub URL is stale → every packet silently spools, the brain receives nothing, and the live demo shows an empty memory with NO error surfaced to the user (the spool succeeds). The whole engine appears 'working' while capturing into a void.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the mean-time-to-misconfiguration in real use (IP changes, network switches), and does mDNS/Bonjour auto-discovery eliminate the silent-spool-on-bad-URL failure? Measure: how often does a session start with a stale hub URL, and is there any user-visible liveness signal distinguishing 'streaming to hub' from 'spooling because hub unreachable'?
- **Current-tech hook:** Bonjour/NWBrowser gives zero-config LAN discovery on iOS today; the device→Mac binding should be auto-discovered + a visible 2-light liveness (mirroring the cockpit heartbeat pattern already used Mac-side) so silent-spool-into-void is impossible.

### topology-12 — Enrichment-quality drift between live (bounded) and replay (unbounded) makes memory non-reproducible across topology paths ⚠️
- **Why:** The same captured walk yields DIFFERENT memory depending on path: live, the device runs a thermal/battery-budgeted enrichment ladder (EnrichmentScheduler denies enrichment under pressure, budgetDenied :201); on replay, packets are re-ingested but the budget-denied enrichments were never captured to replay. So the memory you get live (battery-throttled) ≠ the memory you'd get from an unbounded post-hoc pass.
- **Failure if ignored:** A question answerable from a richly-enriched replay is unanswerable from the live-throttled run (or vice versa), so eval numbers depend on which topology path produced the memory — and a low-battery walk silently yields a thinner, less-answerable memory than a full-battery one. Reproducibility of the 'honest number' is destroyed by device power state.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** How much does answerable-question coverage differ between a battery/thermal-throttled live capture and an unbounded replay of the same scene? Measure eval delta across thermal states (.nominal vs .serious, applyThermalState :111); is the gap large enough that the 'honest number' must be reported per-power-state?
- **Current-tech hook:** ProcessInfo.thermalState budget scaling (.serious → 0.5 factor) directly modulates how many heavy passes happen, hence how rich the memory is. The shippable answer is to ALWAYS run the cheap real-time helpers (OCR/ASR — the validated recall core) regardless of budget, and only let the optional VLM enrichment degrade — so the load-bearing text memory is power-state-invariant.

### topology-13 — Packets are POSTed one-at-a-time over HTTP with per-packet TCP — no batching/backpressure for continuous streams ⚠️
- **Why:** Each perception packet is an independent URLSession.dataTask POST to /capture/perception (ContentView.swift:2431), a fresh request per observation. A continuous ambient engine emits many observations/sec across OCR+ASR+detector+VLM. There's no batching, no persistent connection, no backpressure signal from the brain — and on any failure each packet independently decides to spool.
- **Failure if ignored:** Under a real continuous stream, per-packet HTTP overhead and head-of-line stalls cause packets to back up; the brain (single-threaded BaseHTTPServer, blocking _write_memory) can't drain fast enough, timeouts fire, and packets cascade into the spool — so the live path silently converts to offline-replay under load, exactly when the scene is most active (most salient).
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the sustained packet throughput the brain can ingest before timeouts force spooling, vs. the observation rate of all helpers running continuously? Measure packets/sec capacity of trace_brain_server.py and the rate at which a busy scene generates observations; is batching/a persistent channel needed?
- **Current-tech hook:** A persistent WebSocket or batched-NDJSON-over-keepalive with brain-side backpressure replaces N independent POSTs. The brain is a stdlib BaseHTTPServer (single connection handling) — fine for one packet/few-sec, a bottleneck for true ambient continuous capture.

### topology-14 — Auth token is a hardcoded 'dev-token' — the cross-device channel is effectively open on the LAN ⚠️
- **Why:** The device sends X-TRACE-Token: dev-token (ContentView.swift:2428); the brain requires a token only if one is set, else runs OPEN (trace_brain_server.py:538 'OPEN (set TRACE_TOKEN to lock)'). The continuous stream of the user's fused life-context crosses the LAN to a hub with a placeholder credential and optional auth.
- **Failure if ignored:** Anyone on the same Wi-Fi (cafe, hotel, conference) can POST poisoned perception into the user's memory (corrupting consensus) or GET /ask to read the user's entire context. For a privacy-first product whose moat is 'on-device, nothing leaks', an unauthenticated LAN ingest/query endpoint is a fatal contradiction the moment it leaves the home network.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Is the brain reachable/queryable by other hosts on the LAN today, and what is the exposure? Measure: from a second machine on the same network, can you POST perception and GET an /ask answer with the default 'dev-token'? Then: per-session derived key + mutual auth as the fix.
- **Current-tech hook:** Standard fix: per-pair derived key established at Bonjour-discovery time, TLS on the LAN channel (the web-app path already uses self-signed certs for exactly this). The cost of skipping it is that the privacy story is true on-device but false on-the-wire.


## Failure / adversarial / edge cases (things-not-conceived)

### failure-1 — Correlated-misread consensus collapse (frequency != independence) ⚠️
- **Why:** The honesty moat rests on 'frequency = confidence': a value agreed by >=minrep frames is trusted as structurally-not-a-misread (consensus_recall.py:166, structured_recall MIN_REPEAT_SUPPORT=2). But the votes are NOT independent samples. A still camera, a stable glare, a fixed motion-blur, a consistent font the OCR systematically mis-segments, or an autofocus hunt that repeats the same crop will produce the IDENTICAL wrong read across every frame in the window. _window even explicitly upweights this: identical OCR from a still camera gets vote weight = frame count, never 1 (consensus_recall.py:84,144). So a confidently-wrong read is the EASIEST thing to push past quorum.
- **Failure if ignored:** A systematically-misread sign ('Hans Fischer' for a cursive 'Hauptbahnhof', a 6/8/B/0 swap on a number) is read identically 12 times and emitted as high-confidence truth. The moat inverts: the more the camera stares, the more confident the lie. This is the exact opposite of the intended fail-safe and it cannot be caught by the eval (which uses moving-camera walks where reads vary).
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On a static-camera capture of a known-hard target (cursive, low-contrast, foreign script), what fraction of consensus 'wins' are correct vs. confidently-wrong-with-support>=minrep? Measure the correlation between OCR per-character confidence variance across frames and answer correctness — does low variance (the 'still camera' case the code rewards) predict MORE error?
- **Current-tech hook:** Apple Vision VNRecognizeText exposes per-word confidence; ML Kit does not. The fix requires gating votes on confidence-variance, not frame-count — but the code currently has no access to per-frame confidence inside the tally, and ML Kit (the 6x-faster default) can't supply it at all.

### failure-2 — Substring-folding identity collision ⚠️
- **Why:** consensus_read folds a shorter normalized answer into a longer one when it is a substring, summing votes and keeping the fullest (consensus_recall.py:152-162). This assumes substring => same fact. But '1881' is a substring of '18810' (a misread), '1945' is a substring of 'D-1945 Berlin' (a postcode vs a death year), 'Marie' folds into 'Marie-Curie-Strasse' AND into 'Marienplatz'. Normalization strips all non-alphanumerics (_norm:64) so '188' folds into 'Route 188 closed'. The fold is greedy and order-dependent (sorted by length desc, first containing host wins), so which fact absorbs which is arbitrary.
- **Failure if ignored:** Two genuinely different facts get merged; their votes combine to cross quorum a single fact never would, and the 'fullest' representative may be the WRONG one of the two. A date question gets answered with a postcode that happened to contain the digits. Silent, untraceable, and it manufactures confidence from a collision.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Over a text-rich capture, how often does a substring-fold merge two answers that a human judges to be DIFFERENT facts? What is the false-merge rate as a function of answer length (short numeric answers are the most collision-prone)? Does adding a token-boundary / semantic check before folding reduce hallucination without killing the truncation-recovery win?
- **Current-tech hook:** No current-tech component does this; it is pure repo logic. A MiniLM-CoreML embedding similarity gate on the fold (already in the shippable stack) could distinguish 'same fact truncated' from 'coincidental substring' on-device in tens of ms.

### failure-3 — Date-shaped escape hatch (minrep bypass) ⚠️
- **Why:** A value matching the regex for a 4-digit-year-ish string passes consensus on a SINGLE sighting (support>=1) while everything else needs minrep=3 (consensus_recall.py:165-166). The justification is 'a date NNNN-NNNN is structurally not a misread.' This is false: '1881' read once off a blurry plaque can be '1801', '1831', '1887'; the year is exactly the field where a single-digit OCR error is invisible and consequential. The escape hatch was added to pass specific eval questions (the comments cite day-Q dates) — it is overfit to the 15-Q gold the memory note explicitly warns against re-tuning.
- **Failure if ignored:** Single-frame date misreads bypass the entire consensus safety net and are emitted with full confidence. The one fact-class where humans most trust the device (a historical year, a deadline, a price) is the one with the weakest grounding floor.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On held-out captures, what is the hallucination rate for date/number answers that passed via the support>=1 date exemption, vs. answers that earned full minrep consensus? Is the exemption a net win or a net regression once you stop scoring against the 15-Q set it was tuned on?
- **Current-tech hook:** Apple Vision per-character confidence could replace the regex exemption with a real signal (trust a single-frame date only if every digit's confidence is high). Without it, the exemption is a hardcoded guess.

### failure-4 — Silent per-channel truncation (ASSEMBLER_MAX_PER_CHANNEL) ⚠️
- **Why:** The dossier caps each channel at 10 lines (ask_home.py:1270) after ranking by keyword+semantic overlap. Anything past rank 10 is DROPPED before the LLM sees it, with no signal that it was dropped. In a multi-scene day (130 keyframes) the true answer can sit at rank 11. The ranking is the single point of failure: if the question's distinctive token doesn't lexically/semantically match the line carrying the answer (synonym, OCR garble, abbreviation), the answer is silently outside the window and the LLM confidently answers from the 10 wrong lines it WAS given.
- **Failure if ignored:** The engine answers fluently and wrongly because the evidence was truncated upstream of the LLM, and neither the LLM nor the grounding gate can know a better line existed — the gate only checks what's IN the draft against the corpus, not what was excluded. Recall failures masquerade as confident answers.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the recall@10 of the dossier ranker on a labeled capture — for what fraction of answerable questions is the gold-supporting line actually within the 10 surviving lines per channel? How does that degrade as capture length grows (15 frames vs 130 vs 1000)?
- **Current-tech hook:** sqlite-vec brute-force over MiniLM embeddings (the shippable memory stack) makes recall@k cheap to raise, but brute-force is O(n) per query — at hundreds-of-thousands of vectors the ranking step itself becomes a latency/quality tradeoff that the current fixed cap hides.

### failure-5 — Untrusted web-expansion as a hallucination injection vector
- **Why:** The thesis' single most novel layer (INJECTION expands facts via live web/knowledge lookup) is entirely absent today — but the moment it ships it becomes the LARGEST adversarial surface in the system. A web result is an UNGROUNDED text channel that, unlike helpers, did NOT come from the device's own perception. The grounding gate (G2/G3/structural_grounding:2561) validates answers against _raw_text_corpus — i.e. what was READ on-device. Web-expanded facts are by definition NOT in that corpus, so either (a) they bypass the gate, or (b) the gate refuses everything the web added, making the layer useless. There is no trust model, no source-credibility weighting, no contradiction handling between web and helper observations.
- **Failure if ignored:** A phone number reads correctly, the web lookup returns a wrong/outdated/SEO-spam institution, and the device states it with the same confidence as a direct read — laundering an external lie through the on-device honesty moat. Or an adversary who controls a result (poisoned local business listing, hijacked Wikidata entity) gets the device to assert attacker-chosen facts about what the user is looking at.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** When a web-expanded fact CONTRADICTS an on-device helper observation, which wins and how is that decided? What is the measured rate at which the top Brave/Wikidata result for a captured entity (phone, logo, station name) is wrong or stale, and does the gate let those through? Can a poisoned search result make the device assert a false fact with no refusal?
- **Current-tech hook:** Brave API ($5/1k, 95%<1s) returns ranked web text with NO credibility score; Wikidata is editable by anyone. Neither ships a trust signal, so the trust layer is something this product must build — and the privacy story means every lookup also leaks the user's live context (see lens overlap, but here the failure is correctness not privacy).

### failure-6 — Anchored-read hard-refuse vs. assembler-fabricate fork is binary and brittle ⚠️
- **Why:** ask() routes reading/screen questions with an anchor through consensus_read, and on refusal RETURNS a hard refusal WITHOUT falling through to the assembler (ask_home.py:2761-2767) — explicitly to stop the assembler fabricating. But the fork hinges entirely on (a) anchor being non-None and (b) classify_question landing in ('reading','screen'). A misclassification (a reading question classified 'general', or no anchor supplied because the live path didn't pass one) sends the SAME question down the assembler path that the comment admits fabricates ('Hi kaife', 'IPP Garching', 'Hans Fischer'). The honesty behavior is not a property of the system; it's a property of one classifier + one optional argument both being right.
- **Failure if ignored:** The identical question is honest-refused or confidently-fabricated depending solely on whether the classifier tagged it 'reading' and whether the caller threaded an anchor — an invisible, non-deterministic-from-the-user's-view honesty cliff. Demo-day the founder asks the same thing twice phrased slightly differently and gets a refusal then a hallucination.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is classify_question's confusion matrix on reading-vs-general for real user phrasings, and what fraction of fabrication-prone questions reach the assembler because they were mis-tagged or arrived without an anchor? How often does the live path actually supply an anchor?
- **Current-tech hook:** A small on-device intent classifier (MiniLM-CoreML, <50ms) could route, but any classifier has an error band — the architecture should make refusal-on-low-grounding the DEFAULT for all paths, not a privilege of the reading branch.

### failure-7 — Helper disagreement has no arbitration — last-writer / hardcoded-priority wins ⚠️
- **Why:** Multiple helpers observe the same thing and can disagree: VLM TEXT says one string, Apple Vision OCR says another (merge_ocr makes OCR authoritative over VLM TEXT — trace_live_feed.py:113), detector says 'sign' but VLM caption says 'poster', speech transcript says a name the OCR never read. The only resolution rules are hardcoded priorities (OCR > VLM TEXT) and per-channel ranking. There is no general mechanism that detects 'two honest channels assert incompatible facts' and surfaces the CONFLICT. The thesis claims corroboration-across-helpers (frequency=confidence) but the live assembler 'ranks, doesn't vote' (per the grounding) — disagreement is flattened, not arbitrated.
- **Failure if ignored:** When helpers conflict, the system silently picks one by hardcoded priority and presents it as settled, hiding a real epistemic disagreement that should have triggered a hedge or a refusal. The user never learns the channels disagreed. Mis-binding (attribute from helper A glued to entity from helper B) is the documented failure class this enables.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Across a capture, how often do two helpers emit incompatible observations about the same entity/region, and in what fraction does the chosen answer follow the LESS reliable channel? Does adding an explicit conflict-detection stage (refuse/hedge when typed observations contradict) reduce hallucination more than it costs in coverage?
- **Current-tech hook:** All helpers ship today (Vision OCR, FastVLM caption, detector, SpeechAnalyzer) but each emits in its own format; there is no shared typed-observation bus, so conflict detection requires the unbuilt fusion stage (Observation type exists at observation.py:19 but refutation_cue is never produced).

### failure-8 — Temporal drift / stale-fact bleed across the consensus window ⚠️
- **Why:** The consensus window is +-half=5s around an anchor (consensus_recall.py:113). At walking speed and with the device's own thermal duty-cycling, 5s can span MULTIPLE distinct signs/screens. The window groups by OCR-text identity but has no spatial/scene-boundary awareness: two different plaques the user walked past within 5s both vote into the same tally. The native digest's 'stale-but-remembered' tier (ContentView.swift:2274) explicitly KEEPS facts after they leave view — so a fact from a screen you closed can still be asserted as present.
- **Failure if ignored:** Cross-time leakage: the answer to 'what does this sign say' fuses two signs the user passed seconds apart, or a 'stale-but-remembered' screen value (a price, a name) is asserted as currently-visible after the user moved on. The documented 'cross-time screen leak' failure (the comment at ask_home.py:2747 names it) is structurally enabled by a fixed time window with no scene-change gate.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** How many distinct text targets fall inside a 5s window during normal walking, and what is the cross-target contamination rate of consensus answers? Does a scene-change / location-delta boundary (cut the window when GPS or detector-track set changes) reduce contamination without shrinking quorum below viability?
- **Current-tech hook:** CoreLocation deltas and detector track-set changes (both ship: TraceLiveContextEngines.swift:337, TraceDetectorBridge.swift) could segment the window, but consensus_read currently takes only a scalar time center — no scene-boundary signal is plumbed in.

### failure-9 — Noise filter is a tunable that throws away real text ⚠️
- **Why:** is_noise() (consensus_recall.py:53) drops any line where >60% of tokens are <=2 chars, plus a fixed keyboard-key denylist. This is a heuristic with no ground truth. Real targets are mostly-short-token: phone numbers ('+49 89 ...'), license plates, gate numbers ('A 12'), room numbers, dosages ('5 mg'), prices, stock tickers, chemical formulas, addresses ('5 N St'). The product is literally 'a memory for everything you READ' and this filter blindly discards entire classes of the most decision-relevant short text before consensus ever sees it.
- **Failure if ignored:** The device confidently refuses ('I didn't read that clearly') on exactly the short-token text the user most wants remembered — a flight gate, a phone number, a dose — because the noise filter ate it upstream. A false-negative honesty failure: it looks honest but it's blind by construction, and the blindness is invisible.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On a capture deliberately rich in short-token targets (phone numbers, gate/room IDs, prices, dosages), what fraction are silently discarded by is_noise before consensus? What is the precision/recall of is_noise treated as a noise classifier against human labels?
- **Current-tech hook:** ML Kit / Vision OCR return geometric layout (bounding boxes) that could distinguish a structured number block from scattered keyboard-glyph noise far better than a token-length ratio — but the filter operates on stripped text strings with the layout already discarded.

### failure-10 — Two-misread quorum in structured_recall (MIN_REPEAT_SUPPORT=2) ⚠️
- **Why:** structured_recall — the closest thing to typed-fact fusion — promotes a value to a structured fact at MIN_REPEAT_SUPPORT=2 (structured_recall.py:22, used at :240,269,311,377). Two is the weakest possible quorum: a single repeated correlated misread (failure-1) or two frames of the same glare trivially reach it. For identity/outfit/institution/labeled-ID slots, two correlated observations becoming a 'fact with provenance' means the structured layer the thesis points to as its honesty seed will mint mis-bound identities ('person X wears glasses' from 2 frames where the glasses were on person Y).
- **Failure if ignored:** The structured-fact store — the substrate a future fusion/answer packet is supposed to trust — accumulates two-vote 'facts' that are correlated misreads or mis-bindings, then presents them with attached provenance that makes them LOOK well-grounded. Provenance theater: the citation exists but the fact is wrong.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** What is the false-fact rate of structured_recall slots at MIN_REPEAT_SUPPORT=2 vs 3 vs 4 on a labeled capture, broken out by slot type (identity and outfit binding are the riskiest)? Where is the knee where raising the threshold kills coverage faster than it kills errors?
- **Current-tech hook:** Higher quorum needs more sightings, which the ~1-min thermal-throttle ceiling on continuous capture (A18 Pro ~4-5W sustained) actively limits — you cannot freely raise minrep because the device can't afford to perceive the same thing N more times. The threshold is coupled to the power envelope.

### failure-11 — Stand-your-ground premise check is unbuilt and the eval that 'tests' it is in the eval harness, not the engine
- **Why:** The thesis' headline behavior — the LLM contradicts a false premise ('there was no train, that's a mural') — does not exist in the answer path. False-premise/trap awareness lives ONLY in ask_live.py:30's trap bank (the SCORER), not in ask_home. The engine today either answers from the dossier or emits a canned GROUNDED_REFUSAL/AMBIGUOUS_REFUSAL — a silent refusal, which is NOT standing ground. Worse: the COMMIT prompt (ask_home.py:2282) actively biases the LLM toward answering, with the structural gate as the only net. A false-premise question ('what color was the train you saw?') presupposes a train; the assembler will happily find SOME train-ish token and the gate's G3 only fires on presence NOUNS in the draft — if the LLM answers 'blue' without re-asserting 'train', the premise is never challenged.
- **Failure if ignored:** Adversarial / leading questions ('how fast was the car', 'what did the sign about the fire say') extract confident fabrications because the engine has no machinery to detect that the question itself asserts a fact the evidence doesn't support. The most basic adversarial-user attack (presupposition smuggling) is unhandled, and the eval that 'covers' it is measuring the scorer's own trap bank, not the engine's behavior.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On a held-out false-premise trap set authored independently of the eval harness, what fraction does the engine CORRECT (assert the premise is false) vs. silently-refuse vs. fabricate-an-answer-to-the-false-premise? Today the 'correct' bucket is expected to be ~0% — confirm and quantify the fabricate bucket.
- **Current-tech hook:** Detecting presupposition and refuting it requires comparing question-presupposed entities against the fused evidence packet — which needs the unbuilt fusion stage. No off-the-shelf 2026 component does premise-falsification; it must be built on the typed-observation layer (refutation_cue at observation.py:30, defined-but-never-produced).

### failure-12 — Conservative-gate pass-through fails OPEN on every error ⚠️
- **Why:** structural_grounding is documented as 'conservative & non-regressing: any module or memory dir unavailable -> ASSERT (pass-through)' (ask_home.py:2567-2569); every internal try/except defaults to the permissive branch (e.g. :2588 bc=None on exception, :2658 sup=None). This means the SAFETY system fails OPEN: if entity_graph throws, the binding-ambiguity check is skipped and the draft asserts. If load_observations throws, the phantom-presence floor is skipped. Errors in the helpers or memory files don't degrade to refusal — they degrade to TRUST. Under exactly the conditions where the system is least healthy (corrupt memory, a crashed helper, a malformed JSON channel), the honesty guarantees silently switch off.
- **Failure if ignored:** A subtly-corrupt memory file or a thrown exception in any gate module turns the honesty moat off without any signal, and the engine reverts to the fabrication-prone raw assembler draft — precisely when the data is bad. The system is most likely to lie exactly when something upstream is broken. No telemetry distinguishes 'asserted because grounded' from 'asserted because the gate errored.'
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Inject faults (malformed channel JSON, entity_graph exception, empty corpus) and measure: what fraction of gate evaluations fall through to ASSERT via the except branch, and what is the hallucination rate of those fall-through asserts vs. healthy asserts? Should the gate fail CLOSED (refuse) instead of open when a module errors?
- **Current-tech hook:** Pure repo design choice; no current-tech dependency. The fix (fail-closed + a 'gate degraded' signal surfaced to the user) is free but changes the coverage/honesty tradeoff and would need re-measuring against the gold.

### failure-13 — max(splitlines, key=len) answer extraction picks the longest garble ⚠️
- **Why:** After the LLM answers each frame, consensus_read keeps max(ans.splitlines(), key=len) 'to drop glued OCR fragments' (consensus_recall.py:140). This assumes the longest line is the real answer. If the local LLM returns a multi-line answer where the longest line is a hallucinated elaboration, a restated question, or a glued-together OCR run, the LONGEST wrong line is selected and then normalized and voted. The heuristic optimizes for length, and length is exactly what a verbose/hallucinating small local model produces when uncertain.
- **Failure if ignored:** The vote is cast for the LLM's most verbose line — often the least grounded one — so consensus aggregates over the wrong field of each frame's answer. A model that pads its answer under uncertainty gets its padding promoted to the ballot.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** How often is the longest line of the per-frame answer NOT the intended answer span (vs. the first line, or a regex-extracted value)? Does extracting the answer by a verbatim-substring-of-OCR check instead of by length change the consensus correctness?
- **Current-tech hook:** Constraining the per-frame answerer to copy a verbatim OCR substring (the prompt already demands it, ANSWER_PROMPT:44) and validating that programmatically would beat the length heuristic — but small on-device LLMs (gemma3, the sub-5-tok/s class) are exactly the ones that ignore 'verbatim only' instructions, so the validation must be code, not prompt.

### failure-14 — Empty-tally / empty-dossier silent collapse to generic 'I don't have that' ⚠️
- **Why:** Multiple paths collapse a real failure into an indistinguishable benign refusal: empty tally -> REFUSAL (consensus_recall.py:147), empty dossier -> 'I don't have that in my memory' (ask_home.py:2707), no kf/world -> 'haven't built a memory yet' (:2738). These conflate FOUR distinct states — (1) the thing genuinely wasn't perceived, (2) every helper crashed/produced nothing, (3) the ranker filtered the evidence out, (4) the capture pipeline never wrote the channel — into one user-facing 'I don't have that.' The user (and the founder evaluating) cannot tell a true honest-negative from a silent pipeline failure.
- **Failure if ignored:** A broken capture/ingest run is indistinguishable from a device that honestly didn't see the answer. Eval numbers look like honest refusals when they're actually missing-data bugs; the founder trusts a 'refusal rate' that is partly silent breakage. Debugging is blind because all failures emit the same sentence.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Instrument each refusal path with a reason code; on a real capture, what fraction of 'I don't have that' refusals are true negatives vs. empty-channel / ranker-dropout / ingest-failure? What is the honest-refusal rate AFTER subtracting pipeline failures?
- **Current-tech hook:** Pure observability gap; no current-tech blocker. Distinct refusal reason codes cost nothing and are required before any refusal-rate metric can be trusted as a product claim.

### failure-15 — Tiny-n eval overfit + adversarial gold authorship as the meta-failure
- **Why:** The validated numbers (47%->60%, halluc 42%->~9-18%) come from a 15-question gold the memory note itself flags as 'tiny' and warns against re-tuning. Several mechanisms here are visibly overfit to it: the date-exemption cites 'day Q dates', G1/G2/G3 cite specific Q-numbers (Q13/Q17/Q18/Q20), G4 is DISABLED because it regressed ON THAT SET. The whole honesty apparatus is a stack of per-question patches. Adversarially: the gold is authored by the same party building the system, on captures the system was tuned on, scored by a harness (ask_live) that the memory note flags as having FAKE scoring ('scores any non-refusal as correct'). The measurement chain that certifies the moat is itself the largest unaudited failure surface.
- **Failure if ignored:** The reported honesty gains do not generalize; they are a curve fit to 15 questions on familiar captures. Ship it and the field hallucination rate reverts toward the 42% baseline. The founder pitches a number that was never measured on held-out data, and the gate constants (minrep=3, CONF_MIN=0.6, MIN_REPEAT=2, all the G-thresholds) are coordinates of an overfit point, not robust settings.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On a LARGER, independently-authored, never-tuned-on capture (the 'bigger text-rich capture' the memory note says gates pitch-readiness), do the same constants hold the 60%/<10% numbers, or does correctness drop and hallucination rise? Re-derive each gate threshold's sensitivity curve on the held-out set — which constants are robust and which are overfit coordinates?
- **Current-tech hook:** No tech blocker — this is a measurement-discipline failure. The deferred WebSearch/eval tooling and the device's own capture can generate a larger n, but the binding constraint is human-frozen gold authored by someone other than the system-builder (capture-fidelity finding already notes auto-gold is unreliable).

### failure-16 — Thermal duty-cycling silently changes the perception sampling distribution mid-session ⚠️
- **Why:** Continuous capture throttles in ~1 minute to ~4-5W sustained (the documented hard wall); the device responds by duty-cycling the VLM to key/sharp frames and pushing work onto the ANE. But every consensus/quorum threshold in the system (minrep=3, MIN_REPEAT=2, the half=5s window, seen_count>=3) assumes a roughly STABLE frame-arrival rate. As the device heats, the effective frames-per-target DROPS — so the same physical sign that earned quorum in the cool first minute fails quorum after thermal throttling kicks in. The honesty behavior thus depends on device temperature: the engine gets MORE conservative (more refusals) as a session lengthens, for reasons invisible to the user.
- **Failure if ignored:** A user on a long walk finds the device progressively 'forgets how to read' as it warms — late-session targets refuse not because they were unreadable but because throttling starved them of the frames quorum needs. Worse, the eval (short captures, cool device) never sees this regime, so the measured numbers are best-case thermal and don't predict real sustained use.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Across a sustained (>10 min) capture, how does effective frames-per-target and consensus-pass-rate decay with device thermal state? Do the quorum thresholds need to be adaptive to frame-rate (vote on density, not absolute count) to hold honesty stable as the device throttles?
- **Current-tech hook:** iOS ProcessInfo.thermalState and ARKit's documented capture-frame-rate throttling expose the throttle signal; EnrichmentScheduler's SalienceScorer (EnrichmentScheduler.swift:50) already budgets enrichment — but consensus thresholds are fixed constants, not coupled to the live frame-rate the scheduler actually achieves.


## Evaluation / yield / ambient product

### eval-1 — The gold key is built by the same model class being evaluated (auto-gold circularity) ⚠️
- **Why:** build_clip_eval.py and posthoc_ablation.py derive 'ground truth' from the camera's own OCR/VLM reads (clip_spans only asks about text the camera DEMONSTRABLY read; posthoc judge is an ollama model). The eval can only ever ask questions the helper already answered, and the judge shares the perceiver's blind spots. This silently caps measured answerability at the helper's own recall and makes hallucination on text-the-camera-missed structurally invisible to the metric.
- **Failure if ignored:** Engine scores 60% strict / 67% fair and looks pitch-ready, but the score is a tautology: it measures 'can the LLM read back what OCR already extracted,' not 'can the device recall what was in the scene.' Real-world recall on the founder walk is unknown and likely far lower; the founder ships on a number that cannot fail.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On a frozen capture, what is answerability/hallucination when gold is built by a HUMAN watching the raw video (not from the camera's OCR), split into (a) text the camera read, (b) text in-scene the camera missed? What is the delta between human-gold and auto-gold answerability on the same question set?
- **Current-tech hook:** Apple Vision OCR ~0.31s/frame with per-word VNConfidence — run it offline at full frame-rate on the raw .mov to build an upper-bound 'what was readable' set, then have a human prune to true gold; compare against the live duty-cycled read.

### eval-2 — RAS double-counts hallucination as (correct - wrong), inflating the headline number ⚠️
- **Why:** run_ras.py and ask_live.py both compute RAS = (correct - wrong)/total*100. Hallucination is subtracted once from a numerator that is also a percentage of total, so the same wrong answer both fails to add and actively subtracts — but an honest miss is neutral. This is not a calibrated metric; a system that refuses everything scores 0 (looks bad) while a system that answers half and is wrong on a quarter can look comparable. The metric conflates coverage and honesty into one scalar that hides the tradeoff the product lives or dies on.
- **Failure if ignored:** Founder optimizes a single RAS number and cannot see whether gains came from answering more (yield up) or hallucinating less (honesty up). A pitch claim of 'RAS 60' is uninterpretable to an investor and the engine could regress on hallucination while RAS rises (by answering more easy questions).
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Reported as a 2D operating point not a scalar: at the chosen refusal threshold, what is (answer-yield = answered/answerable, hallucination-rate = wrong/answered) with confidence intervals? What does the full yield-vs-hallucination ROC curve look like as the grounding gate threshold sweeps?
- **Current-tech hook:** Apple Vision per-word confidence + consensus frequency give a tunable refusal threshold; sweeping ASSEMBLER_CONF_MIN/quorum produces the ROC directly from existing data — no new capture needed.

### eval-3 — n is catastrophically small and not held out (15-Q eval overfitting) ⚠️
- **Why:** The memory note flags it explicitly: the 47%→60% win is on a 15-question eval that has been tuned against. consensus_recall thresholds, merge ratios, and the gate were all chosen while looking at these same items. With n=15, one item is ~6.7 points; the entire reported improvement is inside the noise band and inside the overfit set. There is no train/test split anywhere in the eval harness.
- **Failure if ignored:** The 'validated' core is a memorized answer key. First contact with a fresh capture collapses the number, the founder's trust in the metric is destroyed, and the pitch (built on 60%) is falsified live.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On a NEVER-SEEN held-out capture with n>=100 questions, with all thresholds frozen from the dev set, what is answerability and hallucination, and what is the 95% CI? Does the held-out number stay within the CI of the dev number?
- **Current-tech hook:** The thermal/duty-cycle ceiling (~1 min to throttle) bounds how much fresh capture you can get per session — so a trustworthy n requires MANY short captures, not one long one; budget capture sessions accordingly.

### eval-4 — The eval scores a standalone consensus stub, NOT the shipped brain (ask_home.ask) ⚠️
- **Why:** consensus_read is invoked ONLY on the anchored live read path (ask_home.py:2750), not inside the default assembler; the memory note confirms 'not yet wired into ask_home.' The 60% number comes from scripts/consensus_recall.py run standalone with a deterministic answerer stub (test_consensus_recall.py uses date_answerer/name_answerer stubs). real_brain_probe.py exists precisely because nobody knows if the real brain matches. The headline metric measures a module the product does not actually run end-to-end.
- **Failure if ignored:** Founder believes the engine recalls text at 60%, but the deployed ask_home path routes most questions through the flattening dossier assembler (no consensus voting), so the live product hallucinates at the old 42% rate while the dashboard shows 60%.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Run real_brain_probe.py: on the identical question set, what is ask_home.ask's answerability/hallucination vs the standalone consensus eval? What fraction of eval questions even hit the anchored consensus path vs fall through to the un-voted assembler?
- **Current-tech hook:** sqlite-vec + MiniLM-CoreML retrieval at query time means the anchor-routing decision is itself a retrieval step that can be measured — instrument which path each question takes.

### eval-5 — No metric exists for the unprompted-speech decision (when the device speaks on its own) ⚠️
- **Why:** The thesis is Context->Prompt->Answer: the device understands ambiently and may speak BEFORE a query. But there is zero code for proactive surfacing (grep for unprompted/proactive/notify/interrupt in the live path returns nothing real). The entire eval suite is reactive Q&A. The ambient product's defining behavior — deciding a fact is worth interrupting the user for — has no precision/recall, no false-alarm-rate, no measurable trigger at all.
- **Failure if ignored:** Ship an 'ambient memory' product whose only proven behavior is answering when asked — i.e. a slow snapshot assistant, the exact thing the thesis claims to be the opposite of. Proactive speech, if added, will be tuned by vibes and either spam the user (kills trust) or never fire (invisible product).
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Define the surfacing event: on a labeled walk, what is precision/recall of 'moments worth surfacing unprompted' against human-labeled salient moments, and what is the false-interruption rate per hour at the chosen salience threshold?
- **Current-tech hook:** EnrichmentScheduler SalienceScorer + native seen_count>=3 stable-fact tiers already produce a salience signal; A18 Pro's ~4-5W sustained budget caps how often you can afford to surface — the interruption budget is also a power budget.

### eval-6 — Helper ROI / yield-per-watt is unmeasured — which perceivers earn their thermal cost ⚠️
- **Why:** There are 7+ helpers (VLM, Vision OCR, Speech, whisper, location, detector, audio-events). analyze_budget_run.py counts enrichments vs a ceiling but never attributes ANSWER yield to a channel. Under the hard ~4-5W sustained / 1-min-throttle wall, every helper that runs steals duty-cycle from another. No data says which helper actually contributes correct answers per joule. The VLM (sub-5 tok/s, thermally expensive) may contribute almost nothing the OCR channel doesn't already cover.
- **Failure if ignored:** The engine runs the expensive VLM continuously, throttles in a minute, drops frames OCR needed, and the dropped OCR frames were the ones carrying the answerable text — paying the most for the channel that yields least, degrading the channel that yields most.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Per helper, what is (answers-uniquely-enabled / energy-cost) via leave-one-channel-out ablation on a fixed capture? If the VLM is disabled, how much answerability is lost vs how much OCR frame-rate (and thus answerability) is gained back from the freed thermal budget?
- **Current-tech hook:** posthoc_ablation.py already does leave-out scoring; pair it with on-device powermetrics / thermalState sampling (A18 throttles at ~1 min) to get answers-per-watt per channel.

### eval-7 — False-premise / stand-your-ground is only tested as 'refuse', never as 'correct the user' ⚠️
- **Why:** ask_live.py's trap bank scores a false-premise question as correct iff the engine REFUSES (silent canned refusal). But the thesis demands the LLM STAND ITS GROUND — say 'there was no train, that's a mural.' A silent 'I don't know' and an active contradiction both score identically (correct) today. The metric cannot distinguish honest-but-mute from the actual differentiated behavior the product is pitched on, and there is no premise-falsification code to test anyway.
- **Failure if ignored:** Founder demos 'the AI corrects false premises' but the engine only ever emits GROUNDED_REFUSAL; the trap-bank green checkmarks gave false confidence that stand-your-ground works. Live, asked a leading question, it says 'I don't know' instead of 'that's wrong, here's why' — the demo falls flat.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On the trap bank, split the 'refuse' outcomes into (a) silent refusal vs (b) explicit premise-contradiction citing the refuting evidence. What fraction reach (b)? For (b), how often is the contradiction itself correct (not a hallucinated correction)?
- **Current-tech hook:** Observation.refutation_cue is defined in the domain model but never produced/consumed — populating it gives the LLM a concrete refuting fact to stand on; Brave/Wikidata expansion could supply the corrective fact (a number->institution) for active correction.

### eval-8 — Binding/attribution accuracy is not in any score (right fact, wrong entity) ⚠️
- **Why:** Capture-fidelity finding: hallucinations are mis-attribution (attributes bound to the wrong entity), a CAPTURE problem. But RAS/auto_score grade on cue presence — _cue_present does literal token match. An answer that says the right brand bound to the wrong person, or the right ID on the wrong badge, can match a cue and score correct. The single most product-defining failure (the device confidently swaps who-did-what) is invisible to the metric.
- **Failure if ignored:** Engine scores well while systematically attributing facts to the wrong entity; in an ambient memory product this is the worst possible failure (it confidently tells you the wrong person said/wore/carried X) and the eval rewards it.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On entity-specific questions, what is binding accuracy: of answers that assert a fact about entity X, what fraction attach it to the CORRECT entity (vs a competing co-present one), scored against human-labeled entity bindings — not just cue presence?
- **Current-tech hook:** entity_graph.binding_confidence and structured_recall MIN_REPEAT_SUPPORT>=2 already gate on binding; the metric just never reads them — surface binding_confidence per answer and score it.

### eval-9 — The web-expansion injection layer has no yield metric and no privacy-cost accounting ⚠️
- **Why:** Live web/knowledge expansion (phone-number->institution) is the thesis's single most novel layer and is entirely absent. When built, its value must be measured: how many answers does expansion ENABLE that local helpers could not, vs how many WRONG answers it introduces (the web returns a plausible-but-wrong institution). And every expansion query leaves the device — the privacy moat's biggest threat. There is no eval slot for either.
- **Failure if ignored:** Expansion is added, demos beautifully on one phone-number lookup, and ships hallucinating enriched 'facts' from low-confidence web matches while silently exfiltrating the user's continuous context to Brave/Tavily — destroying both the honesty moat and the on-device privacy claim with no metric to catch it.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On a capture with N expandable entities (numbers, logos, signs, station names), what is expansion's incremental answerability (answers-enabled) vs its incremental hallucination (wrong-enrichment-rate), AND how many bytes/queries about the user's context leave the device per session?
- **Current-tech hook:** Brave Search API ($5/1k, 95%<1s, no profiling) for live lookups vs a local Wikidata snapshot for privacy-safe offline expansion — measure answerability of cached-Wikidata-only vs Brave-live to quantify the privacy-vs-yield tradeoff.

### eval-10 — Live latency is proven for OCR only; the answer-path end-to-end latency is unmeasured
- **Why:** latency_sample (build_clip_eval.py) times Apple Vision OCR per frame vs the per-frame budget and declares feasible_live — but only for the OCR helper. It explicitly notes the full VLM caption (~1-3s) does NOT fit. The QUERY latency — from user asks to grounded answer through the assembler + bge-m3 ranking + consensus + (future) web expansion + LLM phrasing — is never measured. An ambient product is judged on perceived responsiveness; the one latency number proven is the cheapest stage.
- **Failure if ignored:** Pitch says 'real-time' citing the OCR 0.05-0.31s number, but a real query takes many seconds through the monolith ask_home.py (2924 lines, bge-m3 embed, LLM decode at sub-5 tok/s for the local brain), feeling like a slow batch tool — the opposite of ambient.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** End-to-end, what is p50/p95 wall-clock from question to grounded cited answer through ask_home.ask (including embedding, ranking, consensus, LLM phrasing), and separately for the proactive-surface path from event to spoken utterance?
- **Current-tech hook:** WhisperKit <0.5s ASR + SpeechAnalyzer set the input-latency floor; the LLM decode (sub-5 tok/s on-device, or Ollama on Mac) is the dominant term — measure the phrasing stage separately since it gates perceived responsiveness.

### eval-11 — Refusals that name the missing channel are not scored for correctness (honest-but-wrong-reason) ⚠️
- **Why:** The honesty moat says refusals must NAME the missing channel (SPATIAL_REFUSAL 'no pose stored', audio 'no usable speech'). But auto_score._is_refusal fast-paths ANY refusal to a pass without checking it cited the RIGHT missing channel. A refusal that blames the wrong channel (says 'no audio' when audio existed and the real gap was OCR) scores identical to a correct one. The moat's load-bearing property — that the refusal explanation is itself truthful — is untested.
- **Failure if ignored:** The honesty story ('it tells you exactly why it can't answer') is unverified; in practice refusals cite plausible-but-wrong missing channels, and when an investor or user probes a refusal, the named reason is fabricated — a meta-hallucination the eval was blind to.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Of all refusals, what fraction name the ACTUALLY-missing channel (scored against which helpers truly had no signal for that question), vs naming a present-but-irrelevant or wrong channel?
- **Current-tech hook:** Each helper already emits a typed refusal (OCR TEXT:NONE, SPATIAL_REFUSAL, audio no-speech); cross-checking the named channel against per-helper presence flags is a deterministic, no-LLM grade.

### eval-12 — Cue-match scoring rewards partial/truncated reads as full correct (no completeness metric) ⚠️
- **Why:** auto_score._cue_present and _matching_cues grade on literal cue token presence with timestamps stripped. consensus_recall's whole value is folding truncated reads into the COMPLETE one — but the eval gives full credit for matching one cue token, so a half-read sign ('Hauptbahn...') scores the same as the complete read ('Hauptbahnhof Gleis 12'). The metric cannot see the exact thing consensus was built to fix, so consensus improvements are partly unmeasurable and partly overstated.
- **Failure if ignored:** Consensus is credited with a win the cue-based metric can't actually detect, OR truncated reads pass as correct and the product confidently returns half-strings as if complete — and the eval says 60% correct.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** For verbatim-text questions, what is COMPLETE-string accuracy (full gold string recovered, not just a cue token) vs cue-presence accuracy? How much of the consensus win survives under complete-string scoring?
- **Current-tech hook:** Apple Vision returns full recognized strings with confidence; score against the complete human-gold string via normalized edit distance, not token-in-answer.

### eval-13 — No demo-script metric for proving Context-FIRST vs reactive (the pitch's core claim is unfalsifiable as built) ⚠️
- **Why:** The differentiator vs Humane/Rabbit/Halo is that context is understood BEFORE the query. But every eval (RAS, clip, posthoc) is query-then-answer — structurally identical to a reactive assistant reading from a log. Nothing measures or even demonstrates that understanding happened ahead of the question. The one experiment that would prove the thesis — answer a question about a moment the user could not have known to log, surfaced from ambient context — has no harness.
- **Failure if ignored:** The founder cannot prove the central claim; the demo is indistinguishable from 'we recorded everything and search it later,' which Rewind/Limitless already ship. Context-first is asserted in slides but the product behaves reactively, and there's no metric to expose the gap until an investor asks 'how is this not just search?'
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** Define a context-first probe: questions answerable ONLY because the device pre-fused/surfaced a fact the user never explicitly attended to. What fraction of such questions does the engine answer correctly, and can it surface them BEFORE being asked (time-to-surface < time-user-would-ask)?
- **Current-tech hook:** Native digest's stable/provisional/stale tiers (seen_count>=3) already pre-fuse on-device ahead of any query — that pre-fused store IS the context-first artifact; build the probe against facts that exist in the digest but were never queried.

### eval-14 — Scoring uses a local LLM judge whose own errors are unbounded (judge != gold) ⚠️
- **Why:** auto_score and posthoc_ablation fall back to a configurable local ollama judge for pending items. A local judge (Gemma/Qwen-class) has its own error rate that is never measured against human verdicts. With n=15 and a judge agreeing ~85-90% with humans, judge noise alone is ~1.5-2 items = ~10-13 RAS points — larger than the reported improvement. The metric's measurement instrument is itself an unvalidated model.
- **Failure if ignored:** RAS movements are judge artifacts, not engine changes; the founder chases noise. A 'regression' is the judge flipping on two borderline items, and engineering effort is spent un-breaking something that never broke.
- **Hard question (Phase 2):** On a human-labeled subset, what is the local judge's agreement (Cohen's kappa) with founder verdicts, and what is the resulting confidence band on any RAS delta? Is the reported 47%->60% improvement outside that band?
- **Current-tech hook:** The deterministic fast-paths (_is_refusal, _cue_present, _clear_quoted_mismatch) already bypass the judge for clear cases — measure what fraction of items the judge actually decides, since only those carry judge noise.
